# DTC Ecommerce CRO Agency for Shopify Stores Running Paid Traffic
URL: https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cro-agency
Summary: DTC ecommerce CRO agency for Shopify brands: research, speed, product pages, bundles, checkout, A/B tests and post-purchase upsells built for paid traffic.

[Home](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/) / [Services](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/services) / Ecommerce CRO Agency

        
        Brand Scaling is an ecommerce CRO agency for Shopify brands whose traffic mostly comes from paid social. When you pay for every click, conversion rate and order value decide how much you can afford to spend on ads. A store that converts at 3% instead of 2% can pay half as much again per click and keep the same margin.
Our CRO work is built around the ads. We look at which angle a visitor saw on Meta or TikTok, then make sure the page they land on continues that story, loads fast on a phone and makes the offer obvious. For store builds and rebuilds, see our Shopify growth work at /shopify-agency. This page is about the ongoing testing and optimisation programme.

        
## What does an ecommerce CRO agency do?
An ecommerce CRO agency finds why visitors leave without buying and fixes it. That means research into customer behaviour, faster mobile pages, clearer product pages, stronger offers and bundles, a smoother checkout, structured A/B tests and post-purchase upsells. The result you want is more revenue per visitor, so every ad dollar goes further.

        
        
        
          
## Research before redesign

          Most CRO goes wrong because it starts with opinions. We start with evidence. In the first two weeks we collect what is really happening on the store, then rank problems by how much revenue they are likely to cost.

          - Funnel data from Shopify and analytics: product view to add to cart, cart to checkout, checkout to purchase, split by device and traffic source.
- Session recordings and heatmaps on the top landing pages from paid ads.
- Customer reviews, support tickets and post-purchase survey answers, read for objections and the words buyers use.
- Ad comments and the hooks that win on Meta and TikTok, so the page matches what brought people in.
- A speed and app audit of the theme on real mobile devices.

          
          
          
        
          
## Speed and product pages

          Paid social traffic is almost all mobile and very impatient. We remove unused apps, compress media, defer scripts that block the first view and simplify the theme where it is heavy. Speed work is often the cheapest conversion gain available.
On the product page, we focus on the first screen. The visitor should see the product, what it does, the price and the offer, and the add to cart button without scrolling. Below that, we order the content by the objections we found in research: proof, how it works, ingredients or materials, sizing, shipping and returns. [UGC](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/viral-creatives) clips and before and after images from the ads often belong on the page too.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## Offers, bundles and order value

          Conversion rate is only half of revenue per visitor. The other half is [average order value](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/aov). We test quantity breaks, bundles of complementary products, free shipping thresholds set just above your current AOV, and gift-with-purchase offers. Each offer is checked against [contribution margin](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/contribution-margin) first so a higher AOV does not come from giving profit away.
Post-purchase upsells shown after payment and before the thank-you page are one of the most reliable AOV gains on Shopify, because they add revenue without adding friction to the first purchase. We set them up with products that pair naturally with what was just bought.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## Landing pages matched to the ad angle

          A visitor who clicked an ad about sensitive skin should not land on a generic product page that opens with a lifestyle photo and a paragraph about the brand. The page should pick up the exact promise the ad made. This message match is where paid traffic CRO differs most from general store design.
We map each winning ad angle to a landing experience. Sometimes that is the product page with a different first screen, sometimes a dedicated landing page or advertorial for colder audiences, and sometimes a bundle page for an offer-led ad. Because our creative team ships new angles every week, landing pages are updated on the same rhythm, not once a year.
We judge these pages on revenue per visitor from the ad that feeds them, not on site-wide averages. A page can lift conversion for one angle and do nothing for another, so the read has to be specific to the traffic source.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## Checkout and A/B testing

          Shopify checkout is already well built, so the wins here are usually about removing doubt: clear shipping costs and delivery times before checkout, express payment options visible, trust signals near the button, and a cart drawer that does not push people back into browsing.
For testing, we run one clear hypothesis at a time on high-traffic pages, with a stated metric and a minimum sample before calling a result. Lower-traffic stores test bigger changes, since small tweaks need far more visitors to read. Every test, win or lose, goes into a log so learning compounds instead of being repeated.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## How a CRO engagement runs

          For brands that need dedicated funnels or advertorial landing pages for cold traffic, we build those too, using the frameworks from our sister site FunnelsThatPrint.

          - Weeks 1 to 2: research, speed audit, funnel benchmarks and a ranked list of fixes.
- Weeks 2 to 4: quick wins shipped, such as speed fixes, first-screen product page changes and clearer shipping messages.
- Month 2 onward: a steady testing rhythm on product pages, offers and landing pages, with results reported as revenue per visitor and conversion rate.
- Ongoing: new landing pages matched to new ad angles as the creative team ships them.

          
          
          
        
          
## Who it is for and how pricing works

          CRO pays back fastest for brands with steady traffic, typically doing about $20K to $2M+ a month and spending at least $10K to $20K a month on ads. Below that, there is not enough traffic to read tests and the money is better spent on offer and creative.
CRO agencies usually charge a monthly retainer, a fixed project fee for an audit and rebuild, a performance fee tied to conversion or revenue lift, or a mix. We quote after a [Brand Growth Audit](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/book), where Gaurav reviews your store, ads and unit economics with you. You can check your current numbers with our conversion rate calculator at /tools/conversion-rate-calculator before the call.

          
          
          
          
        
        
## Real results from client accounts
- [Skincare Case Study: $146,184 in 27 Days at 3.64x ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/q4-here-it-biggest-money-making-season-year): $146,184 in 27 days, 3.64x ROAS
- [Dropshipping Case Study: $2.3M at 11.6x ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/finally-built-million-dollar-brand-2022-ending-2-3): $2.3M, 11.6x ROAS
- [Dropshipping Case Study: $491,798 in One Month](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/dropshipping-isn-get-rich-quick-scheme-it-path-building): $491,798 / month, 34% margin

## Proof from real accounts

- 150+ Verified case studies: Agency-wide results across our client accounts ([see the proof](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/case-studies))

        
## Frequently asked questions

### What is a good conversion rate for a Shopify store?
It depends on traffic source, price point and category, so compare against your own past numbers first. Paid social traffic usually converts lower than email or branded search. One clinical skincare store we work with reached a 5.25% conversion rate in a $61,000 month, but a high-ticket store can be healthy well below that.

### How long does CRO take to show results?
Speed fixes and clear product page changes can show up within the first few weeks. A/B tests take longer because each one needs enough visitors and orders to read. Most stores should expect a steady programme over several months, with gains compounding as test learnings stack up.

### Do I need a lot of traffic to run A/B tests?
You need enough orders per variant to trust the result. Lower-traffic stores should test bigger changes, like a new offer or a rebuilt first screen, instead of button colours. If traffic is too low for testing, research-led fixes and before-and-after comparisons are still useful while ad volume grows.

### Is CRO more important than running more ads?
They work together. CRO raises revenue per visitor, which lets you pay more per click and still profit, so ads can scale further. More ads with a weak store just buys more visitors who leave. We usually fix the biggest store leaks first, then increase spend once the page can hold it.

### What are post-purchase upsells?
A post-purchase upsell is an offer shown after the customer has paid but before the thank-you page, which they can add with one click without re-entering payment details. Because the first order is already complete, it adds order value without risking the original sale. It works best with products that pair with the first purchase.

### Can you do CRO without rebuilding my store?
Yes. Most CRO work happens on the existing theme: speed clean-up, product page changes, offers, cart and checkout improvements and testing. A rebuild only makes sense when the theme is so slow or rigid that it blocks the changes. We tell you which applies after the audit.

# Klaviyo Agency for DTC Brands That Pay for Every New Customer
URL: https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/klaviyo-email-sms-agency
Summary: Klaviyo agency for DTC brands: email and SMS flows, campaigns, segmentation and deliverability built to lift LTV so your paid ads can afford a higher CAC.

[Home](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/) / [Services](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/services) / Klaviyo Email and SMS

        
        Brand Scaling works as a Klaviyo agency for DTC brands that grow through paid ads. When every customer costs money to acquire, what happens after the first order decides how hard you can push on Meta and TikTok. Email and SMS are where that second, third and fourth order comes from, at almost no media cost.
We set up Klaviyo flows and campaigns as part of the same growth system as the ads and the store. The offers in your welcome series match what your ads promise, the post-purchase flow builds on the product people actually bought, and the reporting ties back to [customer lifetime value](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/ltv) rather than open rates.

        
## What does a Klaviyo agency do?
A Klaviyo agency builds and runs your email and SMS programme inside Klaviyo: automated flows such as welcome, abandoned cart and post-purchase, regular campaigns, audience segmentation and deliverability. The goal is more repeat orders and higher customer lifetime value, which lets your paid acquisition spend more per new customer and still be profitable.

        
        
        
          
## Why retention decides how much you can spend on ads

          The maximum you can pay to acquire a customer is set by what that customer is worth over time, not by the first order alone. If a first order makes you $30 in [contribution margin](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/contribution-margin) and a typical customer orders again twice within a year, the customer may be worth well over double that first order. That gap is the room your ads have to scale.
In practice, a stronger email and SMS programme means you can accept a higher first-order CAC on Meta, bid into more expensive audiences and placements, and still hit your profit target over 60, 90 or 180 days. We report new-customer CAC and repeat revenue side by side so you can see that trade clearly. You can model it with our LTV calculator at /tools/ltv-calculator.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## The Klaviyo flows we build first

          Flows run automatically on customer behaviour and do most of the work in a healthy Klaviyo account. We build or rebuild these, with email and SMS steps coordinated so people are not hit twice with the same message.

          - Welcome series: the first-order offer, the brand story, the key reasons to buy and the objections your ads raise, sent over the first days after sign-up.
- Abandoned checkout: people who entered checkout and left, with reminders and, only if margin allows, a light incentive later in the sequence.
- Abandoned cart: shoppers who added a product but did not start checkout, using product images and reviews.
- Browse abandonment: viewers of a product page who did not add to cart, kept short and helpful.
- Post-purchase: order confirmation, how to use the product, what to expect, a review request and cross-sells that fit.
- Replenishment: timed to when a consumable product runs out, which suits skincare, supplements and similar categories.
- Win-back: customers who have not ordered for longer than your normal repeat cycle, with a reason to return.

          
          
          
        
          
## Campaigns and segmentation

          Flows catch behaviour; campaigns create demand. We plan a monthly calendar of product launches, education, social proof, restocks and promotions, with [BFCM](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/blog/bfcm-meta-ads-playbook) and Q4 planned well ahead.
Segmentation decides who gets what. Engaged subscribers who have never bought get different messages from repeat customers. VIPs see launches first. People who bought one product get content about the products that pair with it. Sending to fewer, more engaged people usually earns more revenue per send and protects your sender reputation.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## Deliverability and list health

          None of this matters if emails land in spam. We check that your sending domain is authenticated, warm up new sending domains gradually, suppress subscribers who have stopped engaging, and watch bounce and spam complaint rates. Pop-ups and sign-up forms are set up to collect real addresses and SMS consent properly, rather than filling the list with people who never open.
For SMS, we keep frequency lower than email and use it for messages that are time-sensitive or high value, such as cart recovery, launches and limited offers.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## Measuring email and SMS honestly

          Klaviyo's default attribution credits a sale to an email if the customer opened or clicked within a set window before buying. That is useful, but it overlaps with paid ads. A customer can click a Meta ad, get a cart reminder, then buy, and both channels will claim the order.
We report email and SMS in three ways so the numbers are not flattering by accident. First, flow and campaign revenue inside Klaviyo, read against Shopify orders. Second, repeat purchase rate and time between orders by cohort, which show whether customers are actually coming back more. Third, a holdout on key flows where traffic allows, so a small group does not receive the flow and the difference shows the real lift. The last one is the number that should change how much you let your ads spend per new customer.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## How a Klaviyo engagement runs

          Our wider approach to keeping customers, beyond email and SMS, is covered on our [retention marketing](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/retention-marketing-agency) page at /retention-marketing-agency.

          - Weeks 1 to 2: account audit covering flows, segments, forms, deliverability settings and how Klaviyo revenue compares with Shopify orders.
- Weeks 2 to 6: core flows rebuilt in order of revenue impact, starting with welcome and abandoned checkout.
- Month 2 onward: campaign calendar running, flow tests on timing, offers and content, and segmentation refined.
- Ongoing: retention reporting on repeat purchase rate and LTV, shared with the paid team so CAC targets reflect it.

          
          
          
        
          
## Pricing and fit

          Klaviyo agencies usually charge a monthly retainer, a project fee for the initial flow build, a share of email and SMS revenue, or a mix. Klaviyo's own subscription is billed separately by Klaviyo. We quote after a [Brand Growth Audit](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/book) with Gaurav.
This service fits brands with a product people buy more than once, or a range wide enough to cross-sell, typically doing about $20K to $2M+ a month. We have not published email or SMS [case studies](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/case-studies), so we will not promise you a percentage of revenue from Klaviyo. In the audit we show you what your current flows are missing and what we would build first.

## Frequently asked questions

### Which Klaviyo flows should a Shopify store set up first?
Start with the flows closest to a purchase: welcome series, abandoned checkout and abandoned cart. Then add post-purchase, browse abandonment, replenishment for consumable products and win-back. These cover the main points where a shopper is about to buy or about to drift away, and they keep running without weekly effort.

### Should I use email or SMS for abandoned carts?
Use both, coordinated. Email can carry more detail, images and reviews, while SMS gets seen quickly and suits a short reminder. Send them at different points in the sequence and stop both as soon as the customer buys. Keep SMS frequency lower, since subscribers are less tolerant of frequent texts.

### How does email marketing help my Meta ads?
Email and SMS raise how much a customer is worth over time through repeat orders. When lifetime value goes up, you can pay a higher cost per acquisition on Meta and still be profitable, which lets ads scale further. We share retention data with the paid team so CAC targets reflect real repeat revenue.

### Why are my Klaviyo emails going to spam?
Common causes are an unauthenticated sending domain, sending to large numbers of unengaged subscribers, a sudden jump in volume, or high complaint rates. Fix authentication, suppress people who have not opened or clicked in a long time, increase volume gradually and segment campaigns toward engaged subscribers.

### How often should a DTC brand send email campaigns?
There is no single right number. Many DTC brands send several campaigns a week to engaged subscribers and less often to the wider list. The rule we use is to send as often as you have something useful to say, segment by engagement, and watch unsubscribes and spam complaints as the limit.

# DTC Affiliate Program Management, Done for You
URL: https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/dtc-affiliate-program-management
Summary: DTC affiliate program management, done for you: creator recruiting, commissions, tracking, payouts, fraud checks and partnership ads on the best content.

[Home](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/) / [Services](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/services) / Affiliate Program Management

        
        Brand Scaling offers [DTC affiliate program](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/blog/dtc-affiliate-program) management for Shopify brands that want creators and affiliates selling for them but do not have the people to run it. A programme with no one managing it usually stalls after launch: a few early partners post once, codes leak to coupon sites, and payouts become a monthly headache.
We run it as an ongoing channel. If you want to understand the strategy behind scaling an affiliate programme yourself, our guide at /blog/dtc-affiliate-program covers that. This page is about the service: what we take off your plate each week and how it connects to your paid ads.

        
## What is DTC affiliate program management?
DTC affiliate program management means an outside team runs your affiliate and creator programme for you: recruiting partners, setting commissions, tracking sales, paying out, checking for fraud and turning the best affiliate content into paid ads. You get a channel paid mostly on results without having to staff it in-house.

        
        
        
          
## What we manage for you

          The work splits into five areas. Each one is a weekly task, not a setup step, which is why most in-house programmes slip.

          
          
          
### Recruiting
We source creators, reviewers, niche publishers and existing customers who fit your product. Outreach is personal, with a clear offer and a sample where it makes sense. We also convert your best customers and reviewers into affiliates, since they already believe in the product.

### Commissions and offers
Commission rates are set from your [contribution margin](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/contribution-margin), with tiers that reward partners who drive more sales. We decide when to use a flat fee for content, when to pay a percentage, and when a discount code for the audience works better than a higher commission for the creator.

### Tracking and attribution
We set up tracking links and unique codes through your affiliate platform and Shopify, check that orders attribute correctly, and agree attribution rules with you upfront so partners and paid channels are not both credited for the same sale without you knowing.

### Payouts
We review commissions each cycle, remove returns and cancelled orders, approve payouts and keep partners informed. Paying accurately and on time is a large part of keeping good affiliates active.

### Fraud and code leakage
We watch for self-referrals, coupon sites posting partner codes, trademark bidding on your brand name, and sudden spikes from unknown sources. Problem partners are removed and leaked codes are replaced.

          
        
          
## Turning affiliate content into paid ads

          The most useful thing an affiliate gives a DTC brand is often not the sale, it is the content. A creator video that already sells to their audience is proven creative. With the creator's permission, we run it as a Meta partnership ad from their handle or as a TikTok Spark Ad on their original post.
This is where our affiliate service ties into everything else we do. Our paid team already ships 30 to 50+ new creatives a month for partner brands, and affiliate content feeds straight into that testing. Winners get budget, and the hooks that work get briefed back to other affiliates so the whole programme improves. If your affiliates mainly sell through [TikTok Shop](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tiktok-shop-agency), that side is covered on our TikTok Shop agency page at /tiktok-shop-agency.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## How the first 90 days run

          
          - Days 1 to 14: margin model and commission structure, affiliate platform and tracking set up or audited, partner terms written, first recruitment list built.
- Days 15 to 45: outreach and sample waves, onboarding kits with product facts, hooks and do and do not guidance, first content reviewed for ad use.
- Days 45 to 90: commissions adjusted by partner performance, top content tested as partnership ads and [Spark Ads](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tiktok-ads-agency), inactive partners re-engaged or removed.
- Day 90 onward: recruitment scaled toward partner profiles that sell, monthly reporting on affiliate revenue, cost per order and content used in ads.

          
          
          
        
          
## Partner terms and platform set-up

          A programme is only as manageable as its rules. Before recruiting anyone, we write partner terms that cover commission rates and tiers, the cookie or [attribution window](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/attribution-window), what counts as a valid sale, how returns are handled, where codes may and may not be posted, whether bidding on your brand name is allowed, and how long you can use their content in ads.
We work with the affiliate or creator platform you already have where it does the job, or help you choose one that connects cleanly to Shopify, issues unique links and codes, and handles payouts. The aim is that a new partner can be approved, onboarded and tracked in minutes, and that every order in the affiliate report can be matched to a real Shopify order. Clear terms also make the difficult conversations easier, since removing a partner who breaks them is simply applying what both sides agreed.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## Who this is for

          Affiliate management fits brands with a product creators are happy to talk about and margin to share. Skincare, supplements, fitness, fashion and accessories are natural fits, along with any product with a clear before and after or a daily routine. Brands typically come to us doing about $20K to $2M+ a month and already running paid ads, so the content has somewhere to go.
It is less suited to very low-margin products, where commissions eat the profit, or to brands without enough stock to support a spike from a creator post. If you are not sure which side you fall on, the audit will show whether the margin and stock position can carry a commission-based channel before you recruit a single partner.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## How affiliate management is priced

          Agencies that run affiliate programmes usually charge a monthly management retainer, a percentage of affiliate revenue, a performance fee, or a mix. Commissions, samples and affiliate platform subscriptions are paid by the brand on top, so compare quotes on total cost per order.
We quote after a [Brand Growth Audit](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/book) with Gaurav. We have not published affiliate programme [case studies](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/case-studies), so we will not promise you a result for the channel itself. We can show you the paid social results that affiliate content feeds into across our case studies.

## Frequently asked questions

### What does an affiliate program manager do?
An affiliate program manager recruits and onboards partners, sets commission rates, makes sure tracking credits the right partner, approves and sends payouts, and watches for fraud and leaked codes. In our service the manager also reviews affiliate content for use in paid ads, so the programme feeds your creative testing.

### How much commission should a DTC affiliate program pay?
Base it on contribution margin per order after product, shipping and fees, then decide what share you can give away and still profit. Tiered rates work well: a standard rate for everyone and higher rates for partners who sell consistently. Paying a flat content fee plus a lower commission suits some creators better.

### How do you stop affiliate codes leaking to coupon sites?
Use unique codes per partner, set clear terms that ban posting codes on coupon and deal sites, and monitor where orders using each code come from. When a code leaks, replace it and talk to the partner. Some brands also limit codes to first orders or set expiry dates for campaign codes.

### Can affiliate videos be used as Facebook ads?
Yes, with the creator's permission. Meta partnership ads run the content from the creator's handle, which often reads as more trustworthy than a brand post. On TikTok, Spark Ads do the same with the original post. Agree usage rights and duration in your affiliate terms before running the content.

### Is affiliate management different from influencer marketing?
They overlap. Affiliate programmes pay mainly on commission and scale through many partners. [Influencer marketing](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/influencer-marketing-agency) usually means fixed fees for planned content from fewer, larger creators. Many brands use both, with influencer work covered on our influencer marketing agency page and affiliates handled as an always-on channel.

# Ecommerce Influencer Marketing Agency for DTC Brands
URL: https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/influencer-marketing-agency
Summary: Ecommerce influencer marketing agency for DTC brands: creator seeding, paid partnerships, whitelisted ads and usage rights, measured on new-customer CAC.

[Home](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/) / [Services](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/services) / Influencer Marketing

        
        Brand Scaling works as an ecommerce influencer marketing agency for DTC brands that want creator content to pay for itself. We run product seeding, paid creator deals and whitelisted partnership ads as one program, and we measure it the same way we measure Meta and TikTok media buying: by new-customer CAC and [contribution margin](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/contribution-margin).
Most influencer programs fail for a simple reason. A creator posts once, the post gets views, nobody can tell whether it sold anything, and the content is never used again. Our approach treats each creator as a source of ad creative and social proof, with the organic post as the first test rather than the whole deal.

        
## What does an ecommerce influencer marketing agency do?
An ecommerce influencer marketing agency finds, briefs and pays creators to feature your product, then turns the best posts into paid ads through whitelisting or partnership ads. A good one secures usage rights up front and judges every creator on the new customers and CAC their content drives, not on likes or reach.

        
        
        
          
## What an influencer program with us includes

          The work covers four connected pieces. Each one feeds the next, so a creator who performs organically can move into paid amplification without renegotiating from scratch.

          - Product seeding: sending product to a wide list of relevant creators with no posting obligation, to find who genuinely likes it and who converts.
- Paid creator partnerships: flat-fee or hybrid deals with creators whose audience matches your buyer, with a clear brief and deliverables.
- Whitelisting and partnership ads: running the best creator posts as paid ads from the creator's handle on Meta, and as [Spark Ads](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tiktok-ads-agency) on TikTok.
- Usage rights: written terms for how long and where you can run each video in paid ads, on your site and in email.

          
          
          
        
          
## Influencer marketing vs affiliates vs UGC

          These three get confused, and the confusion leads to the wrong budget in the wrong place. Influencer marketing pays for a creator's audience and credibility. An [affiliate program](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/blog/dtc-affiliate-program) pays a commission on tracked sales and suits creators who want an ongoing income from your product, which is a separate service we cover on our DTC [affiliate program management](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/dtc-affiliate-program-management) page. [UGC production](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/blog/scale-ugc-production) pays creators for content only, filmed to a script for your own ad account, with no expectation that they post it. Our guide to scaling [UGC](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/viral-creatives) production explains how that pipeline works.
In practice the three overlap. A seeded creator can become an affiliate, and a paid influencer post often becomes your best UGC-style ad once it is whitelisted. We plan them together so the same creator is not paid three times for the same video.

          
          ModelWhat you pay forBest used forInfluencer partnershipAudience reach and the creator's endorsementLaunches, awareness in a new niche, social proofAffiliate programCommission on tracked salesAlways-on revenue from creators who already sellUGC productionThe video file and its rightsHigh-volume ad creative for testing
          
          
        
          
## How we run a creator program

          The process follows the same discipline as our paid media work: small tests first, scale only what the numbers support.

          
          
          
### 1. Creator selection
We shortlist creators by audience fit, content quality and how natural their sponsored posts look, not by follower count. Comment quality and the share of real buyer questions tell you more than a big number on the profile.

### 2. Seeding and first posts
A seeding round shows which creators post without being paid and which videos get saves, comments and link clicks. Those creators get the first paid offers.

### 3. Briefs that sell
Each brief gives the creator one angle, the problem the product solves, the proof points and the offer, while leaving the delivery in their own voice. Briefs that dictate every word produce content that looks like an ad and performs like one.

### 4. Whitelisting and paid amplification
The posts that show buying intent are run as partnership ads, with your spend behind the creator's name. This is where most of the measurable return sits, because you control the budget, the audience and the landing page.

          
        
          
## Measuring creators on new-customer CAC

          Views and engagement rate are easy to report and hard to bank. We set every creator up with a unique code and link, and once their content runs as an ad it is tracked inside the ad account like any other creative. The question for each creator is simple: what did it cost to acquire a new customer through their content, and is that below the CAC your margin allows?
To answer it, total cost includes the fee, product, shipping and the ad spend behind whitelisted posts. We compare that against the break-even CAC from your unit economics and against blended [MER](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/mer), because creator content also lifts branded search and direct traffic that discount codes never capture. Creators who clear the bar get repeat deals and longer usage rights. Creators who do not are thanked and dropped.

          - Unique discount code and tracked link per creator
- Whitelisted posts reported as their own ads, on cost per purchase
- All-in cost per creator: fee, product, shipping and amplification spend
- Weekly read on new-customer CAC and blended MER

          
          
          
        
          
## Usage rights, contracts and pricing models

          Usage rights decide how much value you get from a creator deal. Without them, a video that converts brilliantly as an organic post cannot legally run in your ads. We agree the term (for example 30, 90 or 180 days), the channels, whether whitelisting access is included and whether you can edit the footage into new cuts, before any product ships.
Creator fees are usually flat per deliverable, a flat fee plus commission, or product only for seeding. Agency fees for running the program are typically a monthly retainer, sometimes combined with a share of the amplification budget. We quote after the [Brand Growth Audit](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/book), once we know your category, margin and how many creators the program needs.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## Who this is for

          Influencer programs work best for brands with product-market fit, a product that films well and enough margin to pay creators and still acquire customers profitably. Our typical partners do about $20K to $2M+ a month and already run paid social, so creator content has an ad account ready to amplify it.
We do not publish influencer program results, so we will not promise any. What we can show is the creative and media buying system behind it: 30 to 50+ new creatives a month across our client accounts, $50M+ in Meta ad spend managed, and the published [case studies](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/case-studies) where creator-style video ads did the selling.

## Frequently asked questions

### How much does an influencer marketing agency cost for ecommerce?
Agency fees are usually a monthly retainer, sometimes with a share of the paid amplification budget, and creator fees are paid on top. Creator costs vary with audience size, deliverables and usage rights. Brand Scaling does not publish a price; we scope the program after a Brand Growth Audit, once we know your margin, category and the number of creators needed.

### What is the difference between whitelisting and partnership ads?
Whitelisting is the general practice of running ads through a creator's identity with their permission. On Meta this is now done with partnership ads, where the ad shows both the creator's handle and your brand. On TikTok the equivalent is Spark Ads. In each case you control spend and targeting while the post keeps the creator's credibility.

### Should I pay influencers a flat fee or commission?
Flat fees suit creators with proven conversion history and clear deliverables. Commission or affiliate deals suit creators who want ongoing income and lower your upfront risk. A hybrid, a smaller flat fee plus commission, often works best for first deals. Whatever the model, agree usage rights and whitelisting access in the same contract.

### How do you measure influencer marketing ROI?
We add up the full cost of each creator, including fee, product, shipping and ad spend behind whitelisted posts, and divide by the new customers their content drives through codes, links and ad tracking. That gives a creator-level CAC to compare with your break-even CAC, alongside blended MER to catch sales codes miss.

### Are micro influencers better than big influencers for DTC brands?
For most DTC brands, a group of smaller creators with engaged, relevant audiences gives more tests and more usable ad content than one large creator. Smaller creators are cheaper per video and more willing to grant usage rights. Larger creators can make sense for launches once smaller tests have proven the angle.

### Do I need usage rights to run influencer content as ads?
Yes. Posting on their own profile does not give you the right to run a creator's video in your ads, on your site or in email. Usage rights should state the channels, the length of the term and whether you can edit the footage. Without them, your best-performing creator content cannot be scaled.

        
## Related

# Ecommerce Creative Strategy for Paid Social
URL: https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/creative-strategy-agency
Summary: Ecommerce creative strategy for DTC ad accounts: angle research, a 45+ hook and angle matrix, briefs, weekly testing and iteration on winning ads.

[Home](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/) / [Services](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/services) / Creative Strategy

        
        Ecommerce creative strategy is the part of paid social most brands skip. They hire editors and creators, ask for more ads, and end up with fifty variations of the same idea. Brand Scaling runs creative strategy as its own discipline: research first, then a structured hook and angle matrix, then briefs and a weekly testing cadence that tells us what to make next.
On Meta and TikTok today, creative does most of the targeting. Broad audiences and [Advantage+ campaigns](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/advantage-plus) decide who sees an ad based on the ad itself, so the range of angles in your account largely sets the range of customers you can reach.

        
## What is ecommerce creative strategy?
Ecommerce creative strategy is the plan behind which ads get made: the customer angles to test, the hooks and formats for each, the research that informs them and the testing cadence that decides what to scale. It turns ad production from guesswork into a repeatable system that finds new winners before old ones fatigue.

        
        
        
          
## Angles, not variations

          An angle is the reason a specific customer would buy: a problem, a desire, an objection overcome or a moment in their life. A variation is the same angle with a different colour, caption or opening frame. Variations help you squeeze an existing winner. Angles find new pockets of demand.
When an account plateaus, the cause is usually a narrow set of angles, not a lack of ads. Adding more variations of the one message that already works only competes with itself in the auction. Adding a genuinely new angle reaches people the current ads never convinced.

          - Problem angles: the pain the product removes, shown plainly
- Outcome angles: the result or feeling after use
- Objection angles: price, trust, ingredients, fit, shipping
- Identity angles: who this product is for, and who it is not
- Comparison angles: against the old way or the obvious alternative

          
          
          
        
          
## The 45+ hook and angle matrix

          Our matrix crosses 5 angles with 3 hook styles and 3 formats, which gives 45 distinct test cells from one research round. Each cell is a different combination of why someone buys, how the first two seconds earn attention and how the ad is built. This keeps testing structured: when a cell wins, we know which variable did the work and can build on it.

          
          LayerExamplesWhat it tests5 anglesProblem, outcome, objection, identity, comparisonWhy a customer buys3 hook stylesBold claim, question or callout, visual pattern interruptHow the ad earns the first seconds3 formatsCreator or UGC talking head, demo or before and after, static or carouselHow the message is delivered
          
          
        
          
## Research that feeds the matrix

          Angles come from evidence, not brainstorming. Before a brief is written we look at what customers say and what the market is already paying to run.

          - [Meta Ads Library](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/blog/meta-ads-library): which competitor ads have run longest, which formats they repeat and which offers they lead with. Our Meta Ads Library guide shows the method.
- Reviews and support tickets: the exact words customers use for the problem and the result.
- Comments on your own ads: objections and questions that point to the next angle.
- Your account data: hook rate, hold rate and cost per purchase by angle, not just by ad.

          
          
          
        
          
## Briefs that creators and editors can execute

          A brief is where strategy becomes production. Ours fit on one page: the angle, the target customer, the hook options, the key proof points, the offer, the format and length, and what the ad must not say. Creators get room to sound like themselves inside that frame. Editors get a clear structure for cuts and text overlays.
Production can sit with your team, with creators you already use, or with SevenFigureStudio, our sister studio for [UGC video ads](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/viral-creatives). Our direct-response creatives service covers how we produce and edit at volume, and the guide to [scaling UGC production](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/blog/scale-ugc-production) explains the weekly production system in detail. This page is about the thinking that decides what gets made.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## Testing cadence and iteration

          Creative strategy only works with a steady rhythm. Across our client accounts we ship 30 to 50+ new creatives or angles a month, released in weekly batches so there is always fresh supply before current winners fatigue.

          
          
          
### Weekly
New batch goes live. Early signals such as hook rate and click-through are read after a few days, and ads with no traction are cut quickly so spend stays on contenders.

### Every two weeks
Winners are judged on cost per purchase against break-even. Each winner gets iterations: new hooks on the same body, new formats for the same angle, and cut-downs for other placements.

### Monthly
We review results by angle and hook style, retire angles that never won, and refresh the matrix with new research so the next month starts from what the data taught us.

          
        
          
## Common creative strategy mistakes we fix

          When we review an account for the first time, the creative problems are usually the same handful. None of them are about editing quality. They are about what the account is set up to learn.

          - Testing variations of one winning ad and calling it a creative test, so the account never finds a second angle.
- Judging ads on [click-through rate](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/ctr) alone, which rewards curiosity hooks that attract clicks but not buyers.
- Killing new concepts after one day, before they have spent enough to show a cost per purchase.
- Briefing creators with a script instead of an angle, which produces stiff, ad-like delivery.
- Running the same offer and claim in every ad, so the account speaks to one type of customer.
- No record of which angles were tested, so the same losing ideas come back every quarter.

          
          
          
        
          
## Who it is for and how it is priced

          Creative strategy suits DTC brands spending roughly $10K to $20K a month or more on paid social, where creative supply is the bottleneck to scale. Below that spend, there is rarely enough data to read a 45-cell test cleanly.
Agencies usually price creative strategy as a monthly retainer, either on its own or bundled with media buying and production. Brand Scaling quotes after the [Brand Growth Audit](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/book), once we know how many concepts a month your budget can test and who will produce them.

## Frequently asked questions

### What does a creative strategist do for an ecommerce brand?
A creative strategist decides what ads should be made and why. They research customers and competitors, choose the angles and hooks to test, write briefs for creators and editors, read the results each week and plan iterations on winners. They connect production to performance data so every batch of ads answers a specific question.

### How many new ad creatives should a DTC brand test each month?
It depends on spend, but the goal is enough new concepts to replace winners before they fatigue. Across our client accounts we ship 30 to 50+ new creatives or angles a month. Smaller budgets should test fewer, more different concepts rather than many small variations of one idea, so each test gets enough spend to read.

### What is the difference between a hook and an angle?
The angle is the reason to buy, such as solving a specific problem or overcoming a price objection. The hook is how the first one to three seconds earn attention, such as a bold claim, a question or an unexpected visual. One angle can carry several hooks, which is why our matrix tests them as separate layers.

### How do you know when an ad creative is fatigued?
Watch for rising frequency alongside falling click-through rate and rising cost per purchase over a week or more, while the rest of the account holds steady. Fatigue hits individual angles too, not just individual ads. The fix is fresh angles and hooks in the pipeline before the decline starts, not a scramble after it.

### Can creative strategy work without UGC creators?
Yes. Strategy decides the angle and structure, and many winning formats need no creator at all: product demos, statics, carousels, founder videos and comparison graphics. Creator content adds trust and a native feel on social feeds, so most matrices include it, but the research, briefs and testing cadence apply to every format.

# Meta Ads Audit for Ecommerce Brands
URL: https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/meta-ads-audit
Summary: A Meta ads audit for DTC brands: account structure, CAPI and event match quality, creative fatigue, bidding and break-even ROAS, with a 90-day plan.

[Home](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/) / [Services](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/services) / Meta Ads Audit

        
        A Meta ads audit should tell you, in plain numbers, why your account is not scaling and what to fix first. Ours is the [Brand Growth Audit](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/book): a one-on-one review of your Meta ad account, creative, Shopify store and unit economics with Gaurav Kapoor, founder of Brand Scaling, who has 12+ years in ecommerce and has managed $50M+ in Meta ad spend.
It is not an automated report or a checklist score. We go through the account the way we would if we were taking it over, because that is what most audits lead to, and we want the plan to stand on its own whether you hire us or not.

        
## What does a Meta ads audit include?
A Meta ads audit reviews account structure, tracking and Conversions API quality, creative fatigue and diversity, audience overlap, bidding, landing pages and unit economics. It shows where spend is being wasted or capped, then sets priorities. Ours is the Brand Growth Audit, a one-on-one review with founder Gaurav Kapoor that ends with a 90-day plan.

        
        
        
          
## What the audit reviews

          Every account is different, but the same seven areas decide whether Meta can scale profitably. We look at each and rank what is costing you the most.

          
          
          
### Account structure
How many campaigns and ad sets are splitting the budget, whether they exit the learning phase, and whether Advantage+ shopping campaigns are used where they fit. Fragmented structures are one of the most common reasons spend stalls.

### Tracking, Conversions API and event match quality
Whether the pixel and [Conversions API](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/conversions-api) are both sending purchase events, whether they are deduplicated, how event match quality scores look, and whether Meta-reported purchases line up with Shopify orders. If tracking is off, every other decision is made on bad data.

### Creative fatigue and diversity
How long winners have been running, how frequency and click-through are trending, and how many genuinely different angles are live. We map your ads against our hook and angle matrix to find what is missing.

### Audience overlap
Whether prospecting, [retargeting](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/blog/retargeting-for-dtc-brands) and lookalike or interest ad sets are bidding against each other for the same people, and whether exclusions are set correctly so existing customers are not counted as new ones.

### Bidding and budgets
Whether lowest cost, cost caps or [bid caps](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/why-your-facebook-ads-aren-scaling-fix-these-manual-bidding) suit your margin and spend level, how budgets are being raised, and whether scaling steps are triggering cost spikes.

### Landing pages
Mobile speed, product page clarity, offer and bundle structure, and whether the page matches the promise in the ad. Paid traffic cannot convert better than the page it lands on.

### Unit economics and break-even ROAS
Gross margin, shipping, fees and AOV, turned into a [break-even ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tools/break-even-roas-calculator) and break-even CAC. This sets the real target for the account, instead of a ROAS number copied from someone else.

          
        
          
## What you receive

          The output is a 90-day plan built around the four phases we use with partner brands, so you can see what happens in what order and why.

          - Foundation, days 1 to 14: tracking and CAPI fixes, offer and margin changes, product page fixes and the first creative brief.
- Test, days 15 to 45: weekly creative batches built on the hook and angle matrix.
- Optimize, days 45 to 90: conversion rate, AOV and ROAS work so the account can afford more spend.
- Scale, day 90 onward: budget steps of 20% to 30%, cost caps on proven ads, and new markets or TikTok where they fit.
- A ranked list of the issues found, with the expected effect of each fix described plainly.
- Your break-even ROAS and CAC, so you can judge any agency or in-house buyer against the right number.

          
          
          
        
          
## Who the audit is for

          The audit is built for DTC brands with product-market fit doing roughly $20K to $2M+ a month, usually spending at least $10K to $20K a month on paid ads. That is the range where structure, tracking and creative problems cost real money and where fixing them changes the trajectory of the business.
It is a good fit if ROAS has dropped and you cannot tell why, if spend will not go up without CPA rising sharply, if Meta and Shopify numbers disagree, or if you are deciding between an agency and an [in-house media buyer](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/compare/agency-vs-in-house-media-buyer) and want an independent view of the account first. It is a poor fit for pre-launch brands or stores without consistent sales, because there is not yet enough data to audit.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## What audits usually find

          Most accounts we review have two or three problems doing most of the damage, and they are rarely the ones the founder expected. The most frequent are a Conversions API setup that sends events without enough customer data to match well, a structure with too many ad sets splitting a modest budget, and a creative library where every live ad shares the same angle.
Behind those sit commercial issues: a target ROAS set without reference to margin, an AOV too low to support the CAC the market now charges, or a product page that loses mobile visitors before they see the offer. The audit separates account problems from business problems, because no amount of media buying fixes a margin that cannot pay for a customer.

          It starts with a call. You book through the contact page, we confirm fit, and you grant view access to the ad account, Shopify analytics and any reporting you use. Gaurav then reviews the account and walks you through the findings one-on-one.
We do not publish a price for the audit or for ongoing management. The scope depends on how many accounts, markets and channels are involved, and any management proposal that follows is quoted after the review, as a monthly retainer, a percentage of ad spend, a performance fee or a mix. You see the plan and the numbers before any fee is agreed.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## What to prepare before the call

          A few numbers make the audit sharper. If you have them ready, we spend the call on decisions rather than gathering data.

          - [Average order value](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/aov) and gross margin per order after product, shipping and fees
- Last 90 days of Meta spend and Shopify revenue by month
- Your current target ROAS or CAC, and how it was set
- Any recent changes: new offers, price changes, site rebuilds or tracking apps

## Frequently asked questions

### How much does a Meta ads audit cost?
Prices for Meta ads audits vary widely across agencies, from free sales calls to paid deep reviews. Brand Scaling does not publish a price. The Brand Growth Audit starts with a call to confirm fit, and the scope is set after we see the account. Any ongoing management is quoted only after the review.

### How long does a Meta ads audit take?
Access and data gathering usually take a few days, depending on how quickly view access to the ad account and Shopify is granted. The review itself is followed by a one-on-one walkthrough of findings and the 90-day plan. Accounts with several markets or channels take longer because each one needs its own read.

### What access do you need for a Meta ads audit?
View or analyst access to your Meta Business Manager and ad account, Shopify analytics, and Events Manager so we can check the pixel, Conversions API and event match quality. If you use a separate attribution or reporting tool, view access there helps. We do not need edit access to complete the audit.

### How do I audit my own Facebook ads account?
Start with tracking: compare Meta purchases with Shopify orders and check event match quality in Events Manager. Then count campaigns and ad sets, check frequency and click-through trends on your top ads, look for overlapping audiences and calculate your break-even ROAS from real margins. Fix tracking before changing anything else.

### What is event match quality and why does it matter?
Event match quality is Meta's score for how well the customer information sent with an event, such as email or phone, matches Meta accounts. Higher match quality helps Meta attribute purchases and optimise delivery. Low scores usually mean the Conversions API is missing parameters, which weakens both reporting and campaign learning.

### Do I have to hire you after the audit?
No. The 90-day plan is written so your team or another agency can run it. Many brands do hire us afterwards because the audit shows exactly what the work involves, but the audit is meant to be useful on its own, including a clear break-even ROAS to judge any future media buyer against.

# Ecommerce Retention Marketing Agency
URL: https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/retention-marketing-agency
Summary: Ecommerce retention marketing for DTC brands: cohorts, post-purchase, subscriptions, loyalty, win-back, email and SMS, built to raise LTV and allowed CAC.

[Home](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/) / [Services](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/services) / Retention Marketing

        
        Ecommerce retention marketing decides how much a customer is worth after the first order, and that number quietly sets how hard you can push paid acquisition. Brand Scaling runs retention as part of the growth system, connected to the same unit economics we use to set ad targets, so a gain in repeat purchase rate becomes room to spend more on Meta and TikTok.
Most DTC brands treat retention as a set of [Klaviyo flows](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/klaviyo-email-sms-agency) that were built once and left alone. We treat it as a measurable program: cohorts first, then the moments in the customer journey where people drop off, then the offers and messages that bring them back.

        
## What is ecommerce retention marketing?
Ecommerce retention marketing is everything a brand does to turn first-time buyers into repeat customers: post-purchase experience, subscriptions, loyalty, win-back campaigns and email and SMS flows. Its goal is higher customer lifetime value, which lets a brand pay more to acquire each new customer through paid ads and still stay profitable.

        
        
        
          
## Why retention lets you afford a higher CAC

          If you judge paid ads only on first-order profit, your allowable CAC is capped by one order's [contribution margin](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/contribution-margin). Once you know that customers reliably come back, you can judge acquisition on a longer window and bid more for the same customer.
Here is a simple example. A store with a $60 AOV and 50% contribution margin earns $30 on the first order, so a CAC above $30 loses money on day one. If the average customer places a second order within six months at the same margin, contribution over that window rises to $60. The brand can now pay, say, $40 to acquire a customer and still earn a profit over six months, which opens up audiences and bids that were unprofitable before. Retention does not replace acquisition. It changes the maths acquisition is judged by.

          - First-order margin sets the floor for CAC
- Proven repeat revenue in a fixed window raises the ceiling
- Cash flow decides how long a payback window you can carry

          
          
          
        
          
## Start with cohorts, not campaigns

          Before building anything, we group customers by the month of their first order and track what each group spends over time. Cohorts show how many customers come back, how fast, and whether recent buyers behave better or worse than older ones. Blended repeat rate hides all of this.
Cohort analysis also shows which first products, offers and channels produce the best long-term customers. A discount-led acquisition campaign may bring in cheap first orders that never return, while a full-price bundle buyer from a different angle comes back three times. That insight goes straight back into the ad account, where we shift budget and creative toward the angles and offers that attract customers who reorder, and away from ones that only win cheap first orders.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## The retention levers we work on

          
          
          
          
### Post-purchase experience
The first 30 days after an order decide whether there is a second one. That covers order and shipping updates, how-to-use content, setting expectations for results, and a well-timed replenishment or cross-sell offer. Post-purchase upsells on the thank-you page add revenue to the first order itself.

### Subscriptions
For consumable products, subscribe and save turns repeat purchase from a hope into a default. The work is in the offer, the cadence options, making it easy to pause or skip rather than cancel, and messages that keep subscribers engaged.

### Loyalty and referral
Points, tiers or simple perks give customers a reason to come back to you instead of a competitor. Referral programs turn happy customers into a low-cost acquisition channel. Both are judged on whether they change behaviour, not on sign-ups.

### Win-back
Customers who have passed their expected repurchase window get a sequence that reminds, reassures and, if needed, offers a reason to return. Timing is set from your cohort data, not a generic 90-day rule.

          
        
          
## Email and SMS as the delivery system

          Most retention runs through email and SMS, which is why this work sits closely with our Klaviyo email and SMS service. The core flows are welcome, browse and cart abandonment, post-purchase, replenishment, win-back and sunset, plus campaigns for launches and seasonal moments. Each flow is mapped to a stage in the customer journey and measured on revenue per recipient and the repeat purchase rate of the people who receive it.
SMS is used where speed matters, such as cart recovery and limited offers, and kept lighter than email so it does not drive opt-outs. List health matters too: suppressing unengaged contacts protects deliverability for everyone else.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## How we measure retention

          Retention is easy to over-credit, because many repeat customers would have come back anyway. We look at a small set of numbers and track them by cohort over time.

          - Repeat purchase rate at 30, 60, 90 and 180 days
- Time between first and second order
- [Customer lifetime value](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/ltv) over a fixed window, calculated on contribution margin rather than revenue
- Share of total revenue from returning customers
- Allowable CAC based on proven LTV, fed back to paid acquisition targets

          MetricWhy it mattersSecond-order rateThe biggest drop-off in most DTC customer journeysMargin-based LTVRevenue LTV overstates what you can spend to acquireReturning revenue shareShows how dependent the business is on new customers
          
          
        
          
## Who it is for and pricing

          Retention work pays off fastest for brands with a product people can rebuy, a few thousand customers or more and paid acquisition already running. We do not publish retention or email results, so we will not promise a lift. What we bring is the link between retention and acquisition that most separate email agencies miss.
It is also worth doing before a big acquisition push such as Q4. Every customer acquired at peak CPMs costs more, so the flows, offers and win-back timing that bring them back should be ready before the spend goes up, not built in January.
Retention programs are usually priced as a monthly retainer, on their own or as part of a full growth engagement. We quote after the [Brand Growth Audit](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/book), once we have looked at your cohorts and current flows.

          
          
          
          
        
        
## Real results from client accounts
- [Skincare Case Study: $1.6M in One Year](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/finally-client-touched-1-6m-year-mark-insane-roas): $1.6M in one year
- [Dropshipping Case Study: $2.3M at 11.6x ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/finally-built-million-dollar-brand-2022-ending-2-3): $2.3M, 11.6x ROAS
- [Dropshipping Case Study: $491,798 in One Month](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/dropshipping-isn-get-rich-quick-scheme-it-path-building): $491,798 / month, 34% margin
- [DTC Ecommerce Case Study: $374,103 in 16 Days at 2.82x ROAS on $132,832 Ad Spend](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/new-dtc-client-results-last-16-days-132832-ad-spend-374103): $374,103 in 16 days, 2.82x ROAS

- Brand Growth Audit call (Week 0): A 1-on-1 review of your ad account, creative, store and unit economics with Gaurav Kapoor. Free, and you keep the findings.
- Foundation (Days 1 to 14): Tracking and Conversions API fixes, offer and margin changes, product page fixes and the first creative brief.
- Test (Days 15 to 45): Weekly creative batches built on a hook and angle matrix, read against your break-even ROAS, not platform vanity numbers.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is a good repeat purchase rate for ecommerce?
It depends heavily on the product. Consumables such as supplements and skincare should see far more repeat orders than furniture or one-off gifts. Rather than chase an outside benchmark, track your own cohorts at 30, 60, 90 and 180 days and work to improve each new cohort compared with the last.

### How do I calculate customer lifetime value?
A simple version is [average order value](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/aov) multiplied by the number of orders per customer over a set window, multiplied by contribution margin. Use a fixed window such as 6 or 12 months and real cohort data, not an assumption. Our LTV calculator does the maths and shows the CAC your LTV can support.

### Is retention marketing the same as email marketing?
No. Email and SMS are the main delivery channels, but retention also covers the post-purchase experience, subscriptions, loyalty, referral, packaging and how products and offers are chosen. A brand can have strong email flows and still lose customers if the product experience or second-order offer is weak.

### When should a DTC brand invest in retention?
Once paid acquisition is running and you have enough customers to see patterns, usually a few thousand buyers. Basic flows such as welcome, abandoned cart and post-purchase should be live from the start. Deeper work on cohorts, subscriptions and loyalty makes sense when acquisition costs start limiting growth.

### Should I offer subscriptions for my products?
Subscriptions suit products people use up on a predictable schedule, such as supplements, skincare or coffee. They work best with a clear saving, flexible cadence and easy skip or pause options. For products bought occasionally, a well-timed replenishment or cross-sell flow usually works better than forcing a subscription.

### How does retention affect my Meta ads?
Higher proven LTV raises the CAC you can afford, so you can bid more and reach audiences that were unprofitable on first-order margin alone. Cohort data also shows which ads and offers bring in customers who come back, which shapes the next round of creative and targeting decisions.

# BFCM Ads Management for Ecommerce Brands
URL: https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/bfcm-ads-management
Summary: Done-for-you BFCM ads management: Q4 planning, a creative bank, early access, peak campaign structure, cost controls and a December follow-on plan.

[Home](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/) / [Services](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/services) / BFCM Ads Management

        
        [BFCM ads](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/blog/bfcm-meta-ads-playbook) management is about doing the right work in the right order, months before the weekend itself. Brand Scaling runs Q4 and Black Friday Cyber Monday campaigns for DTC brands as a done-for-you service: we plan the offer and calendar, build the creative bank, run early access and peak week, control costs when CPMs rise, and carry the momentum into December.
If you want the playbook to run yourself, our BFCM Meta ads playbook covers dates, structure and budget by week, and the Q4 ecommerce ads strategy guide covers the wider season. This page is for founders who would rather hand the season to a team that has run it many times.

        
## What is BFCM ads management?
BFCM ads management is a done-for-you service that plans and runs your paid ads for Black Friday and Cyber Monday and the weeks around them. It covers offer planning, a bank of ready creative, early access campaigns, peak week structure, cost controls when auctions get expensive and a December plan to keep revenue going.

        
        
        
          
## What the service covers

          The engagement covers the full season, not just a few days of higher budgets. Each part is owned by us, with sign-off from you on offers and spend levels.

          - Q4 plan: offer, calendar, budget ceiling and break-even targets by phase
- Creative bank: offer ads, gifting angles and urgency cuts produced and approved before November
- Early access: list building and early offer campaigns to bank sales before peak costs
- Peak structure: campaign setup and budget pacing for Black Friday through Cyber Monday
- Cost controls: rules and bid strategies that stop spend chasing unprofitable orders
- December follow-on: shipping cut-off, gift card and post-BFCM customer campaigns

          
          
          
        
          
## Planning starts with the margin, not the discount

          The most expensive BFCM mistake is choosing a discount first and working out the maths later. We start from your unit economics: what margin is left after the offer, what that does to [break-even ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tools/break-even-roas-calculator), and how much spend the business can carry at peak CPMs. A 30% discount on a 60% margin product changes the break-even ROAS sharply, and the ad plan has to be built around that new number.
From there we choose the offer type that protects margin while still standing out, such as bundles, gifts with purchase, tiered spend thresholds or a straight discount where it makes sense. We also agree stock levels with you, because running out of hero products mid-weekend wastes the audience you paid to build.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## Building the creative bank

          During BFCM there is no time to brief, film and edit from scratch. Every ad needed for the season is ready before November starts, with proven evergreen winners recut with offer overlays, new angles for gifting and urgency, and static versions for fast swaps.
We build the bank using the same hook and angle matrix we use all year, so the BFCM ads still lean on angles that already convert for your customers. Across our client accounts we produce 30 to 50+ new creatives a month; in Q4 that output is pulled forward so the season starts with depth rather than a handful of ads.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## Early access and peak week

          
          
          
          
### Early access
In the weeks before Black Friday, we run campaigns that grow your [email and SMS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/klaviyo-email-sms-agency) list and invite customers to an early offer. Sales made before peak week cost less to acquire, and the people who join the list become the cheapest buyers once the main offer goes live. Several of our published Q4 results came from this pre-peak window.

### Peak structure
During the weekend itself we keep structure simple: a small number of campaigns with enough budget to stay out of learning, the strongest creative from the bank, and [retargeting](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/blog/retargeting-for-dtc-brands) sized to the audience you built in October and November. Budgets are paced by day, not set and left.

### Cost controls
CPMs rise across the auction during BFCM. Cost caps or [bid caps](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/why-your-facebook-ads-aren-scaling-fix-these-manual-bidding) on scaling campaigns, daily checks against break-even CPA and clear pause rules keep spend from chasing orders at a loss. Manual bidding has worked well in some of our accounts when automated bidding overspent.

          
        
          
## The December follow-on

          Revenue does not stop on Cyber Monday. December brings shipping cut-off urgency, last-minute gifting, gift cards and the chance to bring BFCM buyers back for a second order. We plan this before November so creative and offers are ready, and we use the new customer list from the weekend as the starting point for retention through email and SMS.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## Reporting and decisions during the season

          Peak weeks move too fast for monthly reports. During BFCM you get a short daily update with spend, revenue, blended [MER](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/mer), new-customer share and cost per purchase against the break-even target, plus the decisions we made that day and why. Platform-reported ROAS is read alongside Shopify revenue, because attribution gets noisier when every channel is running offers at once.
Decisions that change your risk, such as raising the budget ceiling, extending the offer or pulling a product that is running low on stock, come to you for approval first. Decisions inside the agreed plan, such as moving budget between campaigns, swapping fatigued ads from the bank or tightening a cost cap, we make on the spot. After the season you get a written review of what worked by offer, angle and phase, which becomes the starting point for next year.

          - Daily update with spend, revenue, MER and CPA against break-even
- Clear approval rules for budget, offer and stock decisions
- Post-season review by offer, angle and phase

          
          
          
        
          
## Who this is for and how it is priced

          The service suits DTC brands with product-market fit, stock to support a spike in demand and a paid social budget of at least $10K to $20K a month going into Q4. Ideally we start by early autumn, because creative and early access need lead time. Later starts are possible but narrow what can be done.
Agencies usually price seasonal management as a monthly retainer, a percentage of ad spend, a performance fee or a mix. Brand Scaling does not publish prices; we quote after the [Brand Growth Audit](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/book), once we know your margin, offer and how much spend the plan will carry.

## Frequently asked questions

### When should I hire an agency for BFCM ads?
Ideally by late summer or early autumn. Offer planning, the creative bank and early access campaigns all need lead time, and an account needs a few weeks of stable performance before peak budgets. Starting in November is possible, but the work shrinks to managing spend on whatever creative already exists.

### How much should I spend on Black Friday ads?
Set the ceiling from your margin after the offer, not from last year's spend. Work out the new break-even ROAS for your BFCM discount, then plan how much spend the business can carry at higher CPMs while staying above it. Stock levels and cash flow set the other limits on how far you can push.

### Do BFCM ads only run on Black Friday weekend?
No. The season usually starts weeks earlier with list building and early access offers, peaks from Black Friday to Cyber Monday and continues into December with shipping deadline and gifting campaigns. Brands that only spend over the weekend pay peak prices for every customer and miss cheaper sales on either side.

### How do you control rising CPMs during BFCM?
We use cost caps or bid caps on scaling campaigns, daily checks against break-even CPA and clear rules for pausing ads that slip. Early access and list building also help, because warm audiences convert at a lower cost when the auction is most crowded. The aim is profitable orders, not the biggest revenue number.

### What is the difference between this service and your BFCM playbook?
The BFCM Meta ads playbook is a free guide to run the season yourself: dates, structure, budget by week and a creative checklist. BFCM ads management is the done-for-you version, where our team plans the offer, builds the creative bank and runs the campaigns day to day with your approval on offers and spend.
