# Ecommerce ROAS Improvement Agency for DTC Brands
URL: https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/roas-improvement-agency
Summary: Ecommerce ROAS improvement agency for DTC brands: we find why ROAS is falling, set a break-even target from your margin, then fix tracking, creative and offer.

[Home](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/) / [Services](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/services) / ROAS Improvement

        
        When ROAS drops, most brands cut budget or change bids. That rarely fixes it, because the cause is usually somewhere else: purchases Meta is not seeing, ads that have run too long, an offer that does not lift order value, or a product page that loses mobile visitors. We start with a [Brand Growth Audit](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/book) to find which of these is costing you the most, then fix it with you.
Every target we set starts from your [break-even ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tools/break-even-roas-calculator), the return at which an order stops losing money after product cost, shipping, fees and returns. Without that number, "[good ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/blog/good-roas-for-ecommerce)" is guesswork.

        
## What does an ecommerce ROAS improvement agency do?
It finds out why your return on ad spend is low or falling, sets a target ROAS from your real margins, and then fixes the causes in order: tracking, creative, offer and landing page, and account structure. The goal is more profit from the same spend, not a higher number in Ads Manager.

        
        
        
          
## Why ecommerce ROAS drops

          In the accounts we review, a falling ROAS almost always traces back to one or more of these six causes. The fix depends on which one it is, which is why the audit comes first.

          
          
          
### Tracking gaps
If the pixel and [Conversions API](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/conversions-api) are not both sending deduplicated purchase events, Meta under-counts sales and optimises on bad data. ROAS looks worse than it is, and delivery gets worse because the algorithm learns from fewer purchases.

### Creative fatigue
Winning ads wear out as frequency rises. Without a steady supply of new hooks and angles, cost per purchase climbs and ROAS falls even when nothing else changes.

### Offer and order value
A low [average order value](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/aov) caps how much you can pay for a customer. Bundles, quantity breaks and post-purchase upsells raise revenue per order, which lifts ROAS without touching the ads.

### Landing page conversion
Paid traffic cannot convert better than the page it lands on. Slow mobile pages, unclear product pages and an offer that does not match the ad all lower conversion rate, and ROAS falls with it.

### Account structure and bidding
Too many campaigns and ad sets split the budget so none exits the learning phase, and audiences overlap and bid against each other. Consolidating usually lowers costs.

### The wrong target
Many brands chase a ROAS number copied from someone else. A brand with 60% margins can profit at 1.7x; a brand with 25% margins loses money below 4x. The target has to come from your own unit economics.

          
        
          
## Set the right target: break-even ROAS by margin

          Break-even ROAS is 1 divided by your [contribution margin](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/contribution-margin) after product cost, shipping, payment fees and returns. Below it, every order loses money; above it, ads are profitable. The table shows how much the right target moves with margin.
Use the break-even [ROAS calculator](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/roas-calculator) to work out your own number before judging any campaign.

          
          Contribution margin per orderBreak-even ROASWhat it means25%4.0xEvery $1 of ads must bring $4 of revenue just to break even33%3.0xA common range for apparel and accessories after shipping and fees40%2.5xRoom to scale prospecting at moderate ROAS50%2.0xProfitable well below what many brands target60%1.67xHigh-margin products can scale aggressively at low ROAS
          
          
        
          
## What we fix first

          The order matters. Fixing creative before tracking means judging new ads on bad data; scaling before the offer is right means paying more for the same thin margin.

          - Tracking: pixel and Conversions API both sending deduplicated purchases, with Meta purchases checked against Shopify orders.
- Target: a break-even ROAS and break-even CAC from your real margins, so every decision has a profit line.
- Creative: weekly batches of new hooks and angles on a testing matrix, so winners are replaced before they fatigue.
- Offer: bundles, quantity breaks and post-purchase upsells that raise average order value.
- Landing page: mobile speed, product page clarity and an offer that matches the ad.
- Structure: fewer, larger campaigns and ad sets that exit learning and stop competing with each other.

          
          
          
        
          
## What a realistic ROAS improvement looks like

          Across the 25 Brand Scaling [case studies](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/case-studies) that publish a ROAS, the median is 3.97x and the middle half sits between 3.61x and 4.39x. Those are results from accounts that were already working, not a promise for every brand.
The first 7 to 14 days cover the audit, tracking, offer and product page fixes. Most brands see measurable change in CPA, AOV and ROAS within 2 to 4 weeks of the first creative wave. Anyone who guarantees a ROAS figure before seeing your account and margins is guessing.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## When a higher ROAS is the wrong goal

          ROAS usually falls as spend rises, because each extra dollar reaches people less likely to buy. A brand at 6x on a small budget may make more total profit at 3x on three times the spend. That is why we judge growth on contribution margin and [MER](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/mer) (total revenue divided by total marketing spend), and use platform ROAS to manage campaigns, not to judge the business.
If your ROAS is high but revenue is flat, the problem is usually scale, not efficiency, and the plan looks different: more creative volume, broader targeting and new channels.

          
          
          
          
        
        
## Real results from client accounts
- [Dropshipping Case Study: $2.3M at 11.6x ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/finally-built-million-dollar-brand-2022-ending-2-3): $2.3M, 11.6x ROAS
- [Skincare Case Study: $115,416 in 20 Days at 4.39x ROAS on $26,271 Ad Spend](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/26271-spent-115416-generated-4-39-roas-skincare-brand-crushed-it): $115,416 in 20 days, 4.39x ROAS
- [Supplement Case Study: $137,620 in One Month at 3.89x ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/record-breaking-month-generating-137620-25-revenue-roas-3): $137,620 / month, 3.89x ROAS

- Foundation (Days 1 to 14): Tracking and Conversions API fixes, offer and margin changes, product page fixes and the first creative brief.
- Test (Days 15 to 45): Weekly creative batches built on a hook and angle matrix, read against your break-even ROAS, not platform vanity numbers.
- Optimize and scale (Day 45 onward): Conversion rate and AOV work, then budget steps of 20% to 30% on proven ads while MER and new-customer CAC hold.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is a good ROAS for ecommerce?
A good ROAS is any figure comfortably above your break-even ROAS, which is 1 divided by your contribution margin. Across our 25 published case studies the median is 3.97x, but a brand with 60% margins can be profitable at 2x while a brand with 25% margins needs more than 4x.

### Why did my ROAS drop suddenly?
The most common causes are a tracking change that hides purchases, winning ads fatiguing as frequency rises, a significant edit that reset the learning phase, a price or offer change, or a slower landing page. Compare Meta purchases with Shopify orders first: if Shopify revenue held up, it is a tracking problem, not a sales problem.

### How fast can an agency improve ROAS?
Tracking and offer fixes happen in the first 7 to 14 days. Most brands see measurable change in CPA, AOV and ROAS within 2 to 4 weeks of the first creative wave. Bigger structural changes, such as new creative angles and a rebuilt product page, take one to three months to show their full effect.

### Does a higher ROAS always mean more profit?
No. ROAS ignores product cost and usually falls as you scale. More total profit often comes from a lower ROAS on a bigger budget, as long as it stays above break-even. We judge results on contribution margin and MER, not platform ROAS alone.

### How much does ROAS improvement cost?
The Brand Growth Audit is free. If you want us to run the work, we quote after the audit, because the scope depends on your spend, channels and creative needs. Partner brands typically spend at least $10,000 to $20,000 a month on ads.

### What do you need from us to start?
View access to your ad accounts and Shopify analytics, your product costs, shipping and fees so we can calculate break-even ROAS, and the last 90 days of spend and revenue. The audit call then walks through what is costing you the most.

# Shopify Marketing Agency for DTC Brands
URL: https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/shopify-marketing-agency
Summary: Shopify marketing agency for DTC brands: Meta, TikTok and Google ads, creative testing, Klaviyo email and conversion work, measured on profit, not clicks.

[Home](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/) / [Services](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/services) / Shopify Marketing

        
        Most Shopify stores do not have a traffic problem or a store problem; they have both, and they are usually handled by different people who never talk. The ads team blames the product page, the developer blames the ads, and nobody owns the number that matters: profit after ad spend.
We run Shopify marketing as one system. The same team plans the offer, writes the ads, runs Meta, TikTok and Google, builds the email flows and changes the product pages, and every decision is checked against your [break-even ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tools/break-even-roas-calculator) and your Shopify revenue.

        
## What does a Shopify marketing agency do?
A Shopify marketing agency brings buyers to your Shopify store and turns them into repeat customers. It runs paid ads on Meta, TikTok and Google, produces and tests the ad creative, sets up email and SMS in Klaviyo, and fixes the store pages that lose sales. A good one reports on revenue, new-customer cost and profit from Shopify data, not on clicks.

        
        
        
          
## What our Shopify marketing covers

          Every engagement starts with a [Brand Growth Audit](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/book), then covers the channels and store work that fit your stage. These are the parts we run for Shopify brands.

          
          
          
### Meta and Instagram ads
Prospecting and [retargeting](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/blog/retargeting-for-dtc-brands) on Facebook and Instagram, Advantage+ shopping campaigns where they fit, and a budget plan set from your margin.

### TikTok ads and TikTok Shop
Native creator-style ads, [Spark Ads](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tiktok-ads-agency) on the best videos, and [TikTok Shop](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tiktok-shop-agency) set up so it shares the same offer and margin model as your Shopify store.

### Google Shopping and Performance Max
Merchant Center feeds built from your Shopify catalog, Shopping and [Performance Max](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/google-shopping-ads-agency) campaigns, and a brand and non-brand split so Google does not take credit for sales you would get anyway.

### Ad creative and testing
New hooks and angles every week on a testing matrix, so winning ads are replaced before they fatigue and the account can keep spending at the same cost per purchase.

### Email and SMS in Klaviyo
Welcome, abandoned cart, post-purchase and win-back flows, plus campaigns, so customers you paid to acquire buy again without another ad.

### Store and conversion work
Product page, offer and bundle changes, mobile speed and post-purchase upsells. Paid traffic cannot convert better than the page it lands on.

          
        
          
## Shopify marketing agency vs Shopify development agency

          Both work on Shopify stores, but they are paid for different outcomes. Many brands need both at different times; knowing which one you need saves months.

          
          Shopify marketing agencyShopify development agencyMain jobBrings buyers and grows profitable revenueBuilds, themes and maintains the storeWorkAds, creative, email, offers and conversion testsTheme builds, apps, integrations, migrationsJudged onRevenue, new-customer CAC, MER and contribution marginLaunch dates, site speed and stabilityHire whenThe store works but growth has stalled or ads lose moneyThe store is new, broken or being rebuilt
          
          
        
          
## What we measure for Shopify brands

          Platform dashboards each claim credit for the same sale, so we report from Shopify first and use ad platform numbers to manage campaigns.

          - [MER](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/mer): total Shopify revenue divided by total marketing spend, the number that cannot be double counted.
- New-customer CAC: what it costs to win a first-time buyer, compared with first-order profit.
- Break-even ROAS: the lowest ROAS each campaign can run at without losing money per order.
- [Contribution margin](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/contribution-margin) after ad spend: what is left after product cost, shipping, fees, returns and ads.
- [Average order value](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/aov) and repeat purchase rate: the two levers that let you afford a higher CAC.
- Conversion rate by device: most Shopify traffic from ads is mobile, so mobile pages are checked first.

          
          
          
        
          
## Who our Shopify marketing is for

          It fits Shopify brands with a product people already buy, doing roughly $20K to $2M+ a month, that spend or are ready to spend at least $10K to $20K a month on ads. If your store is pre-launch or has no consistent sales yet, the free calculators and guides on this site will help you more than a retainer, and we will tell you that on the audit call.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## How to choose a Shopify marketing agency

          Ask these questions before you sign with anyone, including us. The answers show whether an agency manages for profit or for activity.

          - Do you report from Shopify revenue and MER, or only from Ads Manager?
- How do you set a target ROAS, and what is our break-even ROAS?
- Who makes the ad creative, and how many new ads do you test each month?
- What happens to email and the product pages, or do we need another agency for those?
- Can we see real results from Shopify brands like ours, with screenshots?
- What is the notice period, and who owns the ad accounts and creative?

## Frequently asked questions

### How much does a Shopify marketing agency cost?
Agencies charge a monthly retainer, a percentage of ad spend, a performance fee or a mix. Brand Scaling quotes after the free Brand Growth Audit, because the scope depends on your channels, spend and creative needs. Partner brands typically spend at least $10,000 to $20,000 a month on ads.

### What is the best marketing for a Shopify store?
For most Shopify brands with a proven product, paid social on Meta brings the most new customers, supported by Google Shopping for people already searching and email for repeat purchases. The right mix depends on your product, price and margin, which is why we start from break-even ROAS rather than a fixed channel plan.

### Do you build Shopify stores too?
Yes. Store builds, redesigns and conversion work for paid traffic are covered on our [Shopify growth agency](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/shopify-agency) page. Most marketing clients keep their existing store and we change the product pages, offers and checkout as part of the work.

The first 7 to 14 days cover the audit, tracking and offer fixes. Most brands see measurable change in CPA, AOV and ROAS within 2 to 4 weeks of the first creative wave, and a stable scaling budget is the goal by day 90.

### Do you only work with Shopify stores?
Most of our partners use Shopify, and our tracking, email and store work are built around it. We can run ads for other platforms, but the conversion and Klaviyo work fit Shopify best.

# Ecommerce Advertising Agency for DTC Brands
URL: https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/ecommerce-advertising
Summary: Ecommerce advertising for DTC brands: Meta, TikTok and Google Shopping ads run by one ecommerce ads agency, with budgets set from your break-even ROAS.

[Home](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/) / [Services](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/services) / Ecommerce Advertising

        
        Ecommerce advertising is not one channel. Meta and TikTok put your product in front of people who were not looking for it; [Google Shopping](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/google-shopping-ads-agency) and search catch people who already are. Most growing brands need both, in the right order, with budgets that respect their margins.
We run ecommerce advertising as one plan across Meta, TikTok and Google, so the channels do not double count each other and every dollar is judged against your [break-even ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tools/break-even-roas-calculator) and your Shopify revenue.

        
## What is ecommerce advertising?
Ecommerce advertising is paid promotion that sends shoppers to an online store: social ads on Meta and TikTok that create demand, and search and Shopping ads on Google that capture people already looking. An ecommerce ads agency plans the channel mix, makes the creative, runs the campaigns and judges them on profit per order, not on clicks or reach.

        
        
        
          
## The ecommerce advertising channels we run

          Each channel does a different job. These are the ones that matter for most DTC brands, and what we use each for.

          
          
          
### Meta ads (Facebook and Instagram)
The main source of new customers for most DTC brands. Broad and [Advantage+ campaigns](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/advantage-plus), fed by a steady supply of new creative, find buyers the brand could not target by hand.

### TikTok ads and Spark Ads
Short creator-style video reaches younger audiences at a different cost. [Spark Ads](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tiktok-ads-agency) let us pay to boost the best organic and creator videos.

### Google Shopping
Product listings with price and image for people already searching. Feed quality, product titles and margin-based bidding decide how well they work.

### Performance Max
Google's automated campaign across Search, Shopping, YouTube and Display. We split brand and non-brand so it does not take credit for sales you would get anyway.

### Google Search ads
Text ads for high-intent searches, including your brand name and competitor terms, where a buyer is close to purchase.

### Retargeting
Catalog and video [retargeting](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/blog/retargeting-for-dtc-brands) for visitors who did not buy, kept small and frequency-capped so it does not take credit for sales that would have happened anyway.

          
        
          
## Which advertising channel should an ecommerce brand start with?

          The right first channel depends on whether people already search for what you sell. This is how we usually decide.

          
          SituationStart withWhyNew or unique product people do not search forMeta adsYou need to create demand; search volume does not exist yetProduct people already search for by name or typeGoogle ShoppingCapture existing intent at a lower cost per saleVisual product with a younger audienceTikTok ads alongside MetaCreator video sells it; TikTok and Meta share creativeBrand with growing search for its nameGoogle brand search plus MetaProtect the brand term, keep Meta creating demandStrong margins, proven ads, flat growthAll three, budget by MERScale across channels and judge the total, not each platform
          
          
        
          
## Ecommerce PPC: where Google fits

          Ecommerce PPC usually means Google Shopping, Performance Max and search ads, where you pay per click. It works best for products people already look for, and it depends on a clean product feed: accurate titles, prices, images, GTINs and stock.
We set Google bids from your margin per product, keep brand and non-brand spending apart, and compare Google-reported sales with Shopify so the account is judged on real orders. For brands whose demand comes mostly from social, PPC stays smaller and Meta does the heavy lifting.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## How much should an ecommerce brand spend on ads?

          Work backwards from your margin and goal, not from a percentage someone else uses. Start with your break-even ROAS, the return at which an order stops losing money after product cost, shipping, fees and returns. Then set the monthly budget your revenue goal needs at a ROAS comfortably above that line.
The free Meta ads budget calculator turns a revenue goal into daily spend, target CPA and weekly purchases, and the break-even [ROAS calculator](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/roas-calculator) shows the floor every campaign must stay above. Partner brands typically spend at least $10,000 to $20,000 a month on ads.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## How we judge ecommerce ads

          Each platform reports its own conversions, and they overlap. We manage campaigns on platform data and judge the business on numbers that cannot be double counted.

          - [MER](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/mer): total store revenue divided by total ad spend across every channel.
- New-customer CAC compared with first-order profit and LTV.
- Break-even ROAS per campaign, from your real margins.
- Creative hit rate: how many new ads beat the current winners each month.
- Shopify orders versus platform-reported purchases, to catch tracking gaps.
- [Contribution margin](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/contribution-margin) after ad spend, week by week.

- Test (Days 15 to 45): Weekly creative batches built on a hook and angle matrix, read against your break-even ROAS, not platform vanity numbers.

## Frequently asked questions

### How much does an ecommerce ads agency cost?
Ecommerce ads agencies charge a monthly retainer, a percentage of ad spend, a performance fee or a mix. Brand Scaling quotes after the free [Brand Growth Audit](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/book), because the scope depends on your channels, spend and creative volume. Partner brands typically spend at least $10,000 to $20,000 a month on ads.

### What is an ecommerce PPC agency?
An ecommerce PPC agency runs pay-per-click advertising for online stores, mainly Google Shopping, Performance Max and search ads, and often Microsoft Ads. Many also run Meta and TikTok. We run all of them together so budgets move to whichever channel brings customers at the best cost.

### Should an ecommerce brand advertise on Meta or Google first?
If people do not yet search for your product, start with Meta to create demand. If they already search for it, Google Shopping captures that intent at a lower cost per sale. Many brands end up running both, with budgets judged on total MER rather than each platform's own numbers.

### What is a good ROAS for ecommerce ads?
Any ROAS comfortably above your break-even ROAS, which is 1 divided by your contribution margin. Across our 25 published [case studies](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/case-studies) the median is 3.97x, but a 60%-margin brand can be profitable at 2x and a 25%-margin brand needs more than 4x.

### How long until ecommerce advertising works?
Tracking and offer fixes happen in the first 7 to 14 days. Most brands see measurable change in CPA, AOV and ROAS within 2 to 4 weeks of the first creative wave, and a stable scaling budget is the goal by day 90.

# Ecommerce Email Marketing for DTC Brands
URL: https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/ecommerce-email-marketing
Summary: Ecommerce email marketing for DTC brands: the Klaviyo flows that matter, campaigns, list growth, segmentation and deliverability, tied to your ad spend.

[Home](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/) / [Services](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/services) / Email Marketing

        
        Every customer you win through ads costs money. Email is how you earn that money back: the second and third orders cost almost nothing to send, and they are what make a higher [customer acquisition cost](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/cac) affordable.
We build ecommerce email marketing in [Klaviyo](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/klaviyo-email-sms-agency) for Shopify brands: the automated flows first, because they run every day without anyone touching them, then campaigns, list growth and segmentation, all planned alongside the paid ads that bring new subscribers in.

        
## What is ecommerce email marketing?
Ecommerce email marketing is the automated flows and regular campaigns an online store sends to subscribers and customers: welcome emails, abandoned cart reminders, post-purchase follow-ups, win-back offers and product launches. Done well, it turns customers you already paid to acquire into repeat buyers, which raises lifetime value and lets your ads afford a higher cost per customer.

        
        
        
          
## The email flows every ecommerce store needs

          Flows are automated emails triggered by what a shopper does. They are the first thing we build, in this order, because each one recovers or creates sales without new ad spend.

          
          
          
### Welcome series
For new subscribers: who you are, why the product works, social proof and a reason to buy now. It sets the tone for every email that follows.

### Browse abandonment
For shoppers who viewed a product but did not add it to cart: the product they looked at, answers to common objections and reviews.

### Abandoned cart and checkout
For shoppers who started to buy and stopped: a reminder, then proof and help, timed over a few days rather than all at once.

### Post-purchase
After the first order: delivery updates, how to use the product, a review request and the next product that fits, so the first order leads to a second.

### Replenishment and win-back
For consumables, a reminder when the customer is likely to run out. For lapsed customers, a reason to come back before they forget the brand.

### VIP and loyalty
For repeat buyers: early access, bundles and rewards that keep your best customers buying from you instead of a competitor.

          
        
          
## Campaigns vs flows

          Flows run automatically on behaviour; campaigns are one-off sends to a segment, such as a launch, a sale or a story. You need both, but in a different balance than most brands use.

          
          FlowsCampaignsTriggered byWhat the shopper does (signs up, abandons, buys)You, on a scheduleBuiltOnce, then improvedEvery week or monthBest forRecovering carts, onboarding, repeat ordersLaunches, sales, BFCM, contentRisk if overusedLow, they are relevant by designUnsubscribes and spam complaints if sent to everyone too often
          
          
        
          
## Growing the list the right way

          A bigger list only helps if the people on it want to hear from you. Pop-ups and sign-up forms are set up to collect real addresses and proper SMS consent, with an offer that fits your margin, rather than filling the list with people who never open.
Paid ads feed the list too: every visitor your Meta and [TikTok ads](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tiktok-ads-agency) bring in is a chance to collect an email, so the welcome flow is planned with the ad creative.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## Deliverability: making sure emails reach the inbox

          Since February 2024, Gmail and Yahoo require bulk senders to authenticate their domain with SPF, DKIM and DMARC, offer one-click unsubscribe and keep spam complaints low. Stores that miss these see more of their email land in spam or get rejected.

          - Send from your own domain, authenticated with SPF, DKIM and DMARC.
- Include one-click unsubscribe in every marketing email.
- Mail engaged subscribers more often and sunset people who never open.
- Warm up a new sending domain gradually instead of mailing the whole list on day one.
- Watch spam complaints and bounces after every campaign.

          
          
          
        
          
## Why email makes your ads more profitable

          Ads pay for the first order; email earns the rest. If repeat purchases raise what a customer is worth over a year, you can pay more to acquire each one and still make money, which lets your ad accounts scale further than a competitor who relies on first orders alone.
That is why we plan email and paid ads together: the ad creative, the offer and the welcome flow tell one story, and we judge both on [lifetime value](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/ltv) and [contribution margin](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/contribution-margin), not on opens and clicks.

          
          
          
          
        
        
## Real results from client accounts
- [Skincare Case Study: $1.6M in One Year](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/finally-client-touched-1-6m-year-mark-insane-roas): $1.6M in one year
- [Supplement Case Study: $137,620 in One Month at 3.89x ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/record-breaking-month-generating-137620-25-revenue-roas-3): $137,620 / month, 3.89x ROAS
- [Dropshipping Case Study: $2.3M at 11.6x ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/finally-built-million-dollar-brand-2022-ending-2-3): $2.3M, 11.6x ROAS
- [Dropshipping Case Study: $491,798 in One Month](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/dropshipping-isn-get-rich-quick-scheme-it-path-building): $491,798 / month, 34% margin

- Foundation (Days 1 to 14): Tracking and Conversions API fixes, offer and margin changes, product page fixes and the first creative brief.
- Test (Days 15 to 45): Weekly creative batches built on a hook and angle matrix, read against your break-even ROAS, not platform vanity numbers.
- Optimize and scale (Day 45 onward): Conversion rate and AOV work, then budget steps of 20% to 30% on proven ads while MER and new-customer CAC hold.

        
## Proof from real accounts
- $1.6M In one year: Skincare brand ([see the proof](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/finally-client-touched-1-6m-year-mark-insane-roas))

- 3.97x Median ROAS: Across 25 published case studies ([see the proof](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/benchmarks/ecommerce-roas))

        
## Frequently asked questions

### Which email flows matter most for ecommerce?
Start with the welcome series, abandoned cart and checkout, and post-purchase flows, because they trigger on the moments with the highest intent. Then add browse abandonment, replenishment or win-back, and a VIP flow for repeat customers.

### How often should an ecommerce store send email campaigns?
It depends on how engaged your list is and how often you have something worth saying. Many stores send weekly; the right answer is the most often you can send while opens stay healthy and unsubscribes and spam complaints stay low. Engaged segments can hear from you more often than the whole list.

### Is Klaviyo the best email platform for Shopify?
Klaviyo is the platform we use for Shopify brands because it syncs Shopify orders, products and browsing data, which the best flows depend on. Our Klaviyo agency page covers how we set it up and run it.

### Do you also run SMS marketing?
Yes. SMS is built alongside email in Klaviyo, with proper consent collection, and used for the moments where speed matters, such as cart reminders and launches.

### How much does ecommerce email marketing cost?
Email is usually part of a wider growth engagement. Brand Scaling quotes after the free [Brand Growth Audit](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/book), because the scope depends on your list, platform and how much of the flow and campaign work is already in place.

# Ecommerce Agency vs In House Media Buyer: Which Should You Hire?
URL: https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/compare/agency-vs-in-house-media-buyer
Summary: Ecommerce agency vs in house media buyer: compare true cost, speed to results, skills coverage and hybrid models to pick the right setup for your brand.

[Home](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/) / [Services](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/services) / Agency vs In-House

        By [Gaurav Kapoor](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/about), Founder, Brand Scaling · Updated 2026-11-05

        The ecommerce agency vs in house question usually comes up at the same moment: ads are working, spend is climbing, and the founder can no longer run the account at night. You can hire a media buyer onto payroll, or you can bring in an agency. Both can work. The wrong choice is the one made on the headline cost alone.
This page compares the two on the things that decide the outcome: total cost including tools, creative and your own time, how fast each gets to stable results, which skills you actually get, and when a hybrid makes more sense than either.

        
## Should an ecommerce brand hire an agency or an in-house media buyer?
Most DTC brands spending under roughly $50K a month on ads get more coverage per dollar from an agency, because one fee buys strategy, buying, creative and tracking. In-house wins once spend is large and stable enough to fund a full team and you want daily control. Many brands end up with a hybrid.

        
        
        
          
## Agency vs in-house media buyer at a glance

          The table below is a general comparison, not a promise about any one agency or hire. Quality varies a lot within both options, so treat it as a list of what to check rather than a verdict.

          
          FactorAgencyIn-house media buyerCost structureRetainer, % of ad spend, performance fee or a mixSalary, benefits, tools, creative budget, your management timeTime to startUsually weeks, with an audit and onboardingRecruiting plus ramp-up, often a few monthsSkills coveredBuying, creative strategy, tracking, CRO, email often in one teamUsually one strong skill; the rest must be hired or outsourcedPattern recognitionSees many accounts and niches at onceDeep knowledge of one brandControl and speed of changesShared attention across clientsFull-time focus and fast internal decisionsRisk if it failsNotice period, then switchSeverance, rehiring and a lost quarterKnowledge retentionDepends on documentation and account ownershipStays in the company while the person stays
          
          
        
          
## The real cost of each option

          The most common mistake is comparing an agency fee with a salary. A media buyer on payroll is only one line of what it takes to run paid social well. The other lines are tools, creative production and the hours you or a manager spend directing the work.
The example below uses round, made-up numbers purely to show the arithmetic. Plug in your own salary quotes, tool bills and creative costs.

          - Count management time: an in-house hire still needs direction, reviews and approvals.
- Count creative: the buyer is only as good as the ads they are given to run.
- Count tools: attribution, analytics and editing software are often missed in budgets.
- Ask agencies exactly what the fee includes, especially creative volume and tracking work.

          
          
### Example arithmetic: in-house (illustrative numbers only)
Assume a media buyer salary of $90,000 a year, plus 20% for payroll taxes and benefits, which gives $108,000. Add $500 a month for analytics, attribution and creative tools ($6,000 a year). Add a creative budget of $4,000 a month for [UGC](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/viral-creatives) and edited ads ($48,000 a year). Finally, assume the founder spends 5 hours a week managing the hire, valued at $150 an hour, which is about $39,000 a year.
Total in this example: roughly $201,000 a year, or about $16,750 a month. Remove the creative line and it is still about $12,750 a month.

### Example arithmetic: agency (illustrative numbers only)
Agencies usually charge a monthly retainer, a percentage of ad spend, a performance fee or a blend. Assume a brand spends $40,000 a month on ads and the agency charges a hypothetical $3,000 retainer plus 10% of spend. That is $7,000 a month. If creative production is included, the comparison is $7,000 against the in-house example of $16,750. If creative is billed separately, add it to both sides.
At $150,000 a month in spend, the same hypothetical fee becomes $18,000 a month, and in-house starts to look cheaper. This is why the answer changes with scale.

          
        
          
## Speed to results

          An in-house hire has to be found, interviewed, onboarded and given time to learn the account before you can judge them. That often eats a full quarter. If the first hire does not work out, you start again.
An established agency arrives with tested processes. At Brand Scaling, for example, engagements start with a [Brand Growth Audit](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/book) and follow a four-phase plan: Foundation in days 1 to 14 (tracking and [Conversions API](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/conversions-api), offer, margins, product page), Test in days 15 to 45 (weekly creative and a hook and angle matrix), Optimize from day 45 to 90 (conversion rate, AOV, ROAS) and Scale from day 90 onwards. The timeline is the point: you know when to expect a read on performance.
The flip side is that an agency needs time to learn your brand voice and customer, and a good in-house buyer who already knows the product can move faster on day-to-day decisions.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## Skills coverage: one person or a team

          [Scaling a DTC brand](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/blog/how-to-scale-a-dtc-brand) on paid social needs more than campaign setup. It needs [creative strategy](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/creative-strategy-agency), a steady supply of new ads, clean tracking, a product page that converts, and usually retention flows that turn first orders into repeat revenue. One person rarely covers all of that at a high level.
An agency spreads those skills across specialists. As a reference point, Brand Scaling produces 30 to 50+ new ad creatives and angles a month for partner brands and works across Meta, TikTok, Google, [Shopify CRO](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cro-agency) and [Klaviyo](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/klaviyo-email-sms-agency). An in-house media buyer can be excellent at buying, but you will likely need a creative producer, an editor and someone for email as well.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## When each option makes sense

          
          
          
          
### An agency usually fits when
- You spend roughly $10K to $100K a month and cannot yet fund a full in-house team.
- You need creative, tracking and CRO help, not only campaign management.
- You want results within a quarter rather than after a hiring cycle.
- You value pattern recognition from many accounts and niches.

### In-house usually fits when
- Ad spend is large and steady enough that percentage fees exceed a team salary.
- You already have creative production and analytics capacity internally.
- Your product or compliance needs require constant internal context.
- You have someone senior who can manage and develop a media buyer.

          
        
          
## Hybrid models that work

          The choice is not always binary. Plenty of brands combine the two once they pass a certain size, and the split can change over time.

          - Agency strategy plus in-house execution: the agency sets testing plans and reviews the account; your buyer runs it daily.
- In-house buyer plus outsourced creative: keep buying internal and use a creative studio for UGC and ad volume.
- Agency for new channels: keep Meta in-house and use an agency to launch TikTok or [Google Shopping](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/google-shopping-ads-agency).
- Audit then decide: start with an account audit, fix the foundation, then choose who runs it.

- [Dropshipping Case Study: $2.3M at 11.6x ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/finally-built-million-dollar-brand-2022-ending-2-3): $2.3M, 11.6x ROAS
- [Dropshipping Case Study: $491,798 in One Month](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/dropshipping-isn-get-rich-quick-scheme-it-path-building): $491,798 / month, 34% margin

## Frequently asked questions

### Is an agency cheaper than an in-house media buyer?
Often at lower spend levels, yes, because an agency fee can cover buying, creative strategy and tracking that would otherwise need several hires. As ad spend grows, percentage-of-spend fees grow too, and at some point a salaried team becomes cheaper. Run the arithmetic with your own salary quotes, tools and creative costs before deciding.

### How do ecommerce agencies usually charge?
The common models are a fixed monthly retainer, a percentage of ad spend, a performance fee tied to revenue or profit, or a mix of these. Each shifts risk differently. Always ask what is included, such as creative volume, tracking setup and reporting, so you compare like with like. Our own pricing is quoted after the Brand Growth Audit.

### How long does it take an in-house media buyer to get results?
Expect recruiting, onboarding and learning the account to take a few months before you can judge performance fairly. A strong hire who already knows your category may move faster. The hidden cost is the time lost if the first hire is not the right fit, because the whole cycle restarts.

### Can I use an agency and an in-house team together?
Yes, and it is common. Typical setups are an agency setting strategy while an internal buyer executes, an in-house buyer paired with an outsourced creative studio, or an agency launching a new channel such as TikTok while Meta stays internal. The key is clear ownership of the ad account and the testing roadmap.

### What should I check before hiring an ecommerce agency?
Look for published results in brands like yours, a clear process with timelines, who will actually work on your account, how much creative they produce each month, and whether you keep ownership of the ad account and data. Ask how they report on blended results, not only platform ROAS.

# Meta Ads vs TikTok Ads for Ecommerce: Where Should Your Budget Go?
URL: https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/compare/meta-ads-vs-tiktok-ads
Summary: Meta ads vs TikTok ads for ecommerce: audience, creative style, buying intent, tracking, TikTok Shop, when to start each and how to split your ad budget.

[Home](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/) / [Services](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/services) / Meta vs TikTok

        By [Gaurav Kapoor](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/about), Founder, Brand Scaling · Updated 2026-11-05

        Choosing between Meta ads vs [TikTok ads](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tiktok-ads-agency) for ecommerce is less about which platform is better and more about which one suits your product, your creative capacity and your stage. Both sell physical products every day. They just do it in different ways.
Below we compare the two on audience, creative style, buying intent, tracking, [TikTok Shop](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tiktok-shop-agency) and budget, then give a practical order for starting each and a way to split spend once both are running.

        
## Is Meta or TikTok better for ecommerce ads?
For most DTC brands, Meta is the better first channel because its conversion optimization, catalog ads and tracking are more mature. TikTok is strong for reach, younger audiences and products that demo well on video, and TikTok Shop adds in-app checkout. Start on Meta, prove profitable creative, then test TikTok with a ring-fenced budget.

        
        
        
          
## Meta vs TikTok for ecommerce at a glance

          This is a general comparison based on how the platforms work, not a statistic about either. Your results will depend on your product, offer and creative.

          
          FactorMeta (Facebook and Instagram)TikTokAudienceVery broad age range, strong with 25 to 55+ buyersSkews younger, growing older audienceCreative styleUGC, statics, carousels, video, catalog adsNative, sound-on, creator-led vertical videoBuying intentDiscovery, but strong conversion optimizationDiscovery and entertainment firstCreative fatigueModerate; winners can run for weeksFast; winners often need refreshing soonerTrackingPixel plus Conversions API, mature attributionPixel plus Events API, improvingCommerce featuresShops, catalog and Advantage+ campaignsTikTok Shop, Spark Ads, creator affiliatesBest first usePrimary acquisition engineIncremental reach and creative testing ground
          
          
        
          
## Audience and buying intent

          Meta reaches almost every adult demographic and has years of purchase data behind its delivery system. When you optimize for purchases, it is very good at finding people who buy. That is why it remains the default acquisition engine for most Shopify brands.
TikTok users are there to be entertained. That does not mean they do not buy, but the ad has to earn attention as content first. Products that are visual, demonstrable, giftable or a little surprising tend to do well. Products that need a lot of explanation, or are bought mainly by older customers, often find Meta easier.
Neither platform captures existing demand the way search does. Both create demand, which is why creative quality matters so much on both.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## Creative style: what works on each

          On Meta, a mix of formats keeps performance stable: [UGC](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/viral-creatives) testimonials, founder videos, problem and solution demos, static images with a sharp claim and catalog ads for [retargeting](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/blog/retargeting-for-dtc-brands). Polished and native styles can both work.
On TikTok, ads that look like ads tend to be skipped. Creator-led, sound-on vertical video with a hook in the first second performs best, and Spark Ads let you boost organic creator posts so the ad keeps the creator's handle and social proof.
The practical difference is volume. TikTok creative tends to fatigue faster, so you need more new hooks per month. A structured system helps: we use a 45+ cell hook and angle matrix (5 angles x 3 hook styles x 3 formats) to keep both platforms supplied without guessing.

          - Meta: test angles across UGC, static and carousel, then scale winners.
- TikTok: brief creators on hooks, not scripts; keep it native and fast.
- Both: retire fatigued ads based on rising CPA, not on age alone.

          
          
          
        
          
## Tracking and attribution

          Meta's pixel combined with the [Conversions API](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/conversions-api) gives strong signal for optimization, and its attribution reporting is well understood. TikTok's pixel and Events API work on the same idea, but many brands find TikTok undercounts or overcounts depending on setup and view-through settings.
Because TikTok often drives people who later search or come back directly, judge it on blended results as well as in-platform numbers. Watch total revenue against total ad spend ([MER](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/mer)) when you add or pause TikTok budget, and compare new customer counts in Shopify.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## Where TikTok Shop fits

          TikTok Shop lets people buy without leaving the app, and pairs with creator affiliates who earn commission on sales from their videos. For products with an impulse price point and strong demo value, this can remove friction that a website click adds.
It also adds work: product listings, fulfilment standards, sample shipping to creators and affiliate management. Treat it as a separate channel with its own plan rather than a switch you flip. Our TikTok Shop work covers setup and creator affiliates; see the TikTok Shop agency page for how we approach it.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## When to start each and how to split budget

          For most brands we recommend this order: build a profitable Meta account first, with clean tracking, a working offer and a few proven creative angles. Once Meta is stable and you have a creative system producing new ads weekly, add TikTok as a test.
A simple starting split is to keep the large majority of spend on the proven channel and ring-fence a fixed test budget for TikTok, for example 10% to 20% of total spend, for a set period. This is a planning rule of thumb, not a benchmark. Move more budget to TikTok only when blended MER holds or improves as TikTok spend rises.

          - Start TikTok first only if your product is visual, younger-skewing and you can produce lots of native video.
- Set the TikTok test window in advance, such as 4 to 6 weeks, so you judge it fairly.
- Scale whichever channel grows blended revenue, in 20% to 30% budget steps.

          
          
          
        
          
## Common mistakes when running Meta and TikTok together

          Most problems we see when brands add TikTok come from treating it as a copy of Meta. The platforms reward different creative and need different patience, so the setup has to change too.
The other frequent issue is judging TikTok too early or by the wrong number. A channel that looks weak in its own dashboard can still lift branded search and direct traffic, while a channel that looks strong in-platform may simply be claiming sales Meta would have made anyway. Decide your success measure before you launch, write it down and stick to it for the full test window.

          - Uploading polished Meta ads to TikTok without re-editing them for the platform.
- Splitting a small budget so thinly that neither platform gets enough data to learn.
- Pausing TikTok after a few days because in-platform ROAS looks low.
- Launching TikTok before tracking, offer and product page are working on Meta.

          
          
          
        
        
## Real results from client accounts
- [Supplement Case Study: $52,000 in 17 Days at 4.51x ROAS on $11,586 Ad Spend](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/it-safe-say-figured-out-make-supplement-brand-print-money): $52,000 in 17 days, 4.51x ROAS
- [Dropshipping Case Study: $2.3M at 11.6x ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/finally-built-million-dollar-brand-2022-ending-2-3): $2.3M, 11.6x ROAS
- [Dropshipping Case Study: $491,798 in One Month](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/dropshipping-isn-get-rich-quick-scheme-it-path-building): $491,798 / month, 34% margin
- [DTC Ecommerce Case Study: $374,103 in 16 Days at 2.82x ROAS on $132,832 Ad Spend](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/new-dtc-client-results-last-16-days-132832-ad-spend-374103): $374,103 in 16 days, 2.82x ROAS

- Foundation (Days 1 to 14): Tracking and Conversions API fixes, offer and margin changes, product page fixes and the first creative brief.
- Test (Days 15 to 45): Weekly creative batches built on a hook and angle matrix, read against your break-even ROAS, not platform vanity numbers.
- Optimize and scale (Day 45 onward): Conversion rate and AOV work, then budget steps of 20% to 30% on proven ads while MER and new-customer CAC hold.

        
## Proof from real accounts

- 4.51x ROAS in 17 days: $52,000 on $11,586 spend, 369 orders, supplement brand ([see the proof](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/it-safe-say-figured-out-make-supplement-brand-print-money))
- 45+ Cell hook and angle matrix: 5 angles x 3 hook styles x 3 formats ([see the proof](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/viral-creatives))

        
## Frequently asked questions

### Should I start with Meta or TikTok ads for my Shopify store?
Most Shopify brands should start with Meta, because its purchase optimization and tracking are more mature and it reaches a wider age range. Start with TikTok first only if your product is highly visual, your buyers skew younger, and you can produce a steady flow of native creator-style video every week.

### Are TikTok ads cheaper than Meta ads?
TikTok can sometimes offer cheaper reach, but cheaper impressions do not always mean cheaper customers. What matters is cost per acquisition and the profit per order. Compare platforms on blended MER and new customer cost over a fixed test period, not on CPM alone, before moving budget.

### Can I use the same ads on Meta and TikTok?
You can reuse raw footage, but the edits usually need to change. TikTok rewards native, sound-on, creator-style videos with fast hooks, while Meta handles a wider mix including statics and carousels. Re-cut hooks, captions and pacing for each platform rather than uploading the exact same file everywhere.

### Is TikTok Shop worth it for DTC brands?
It can be for impulse-priced, demonstrable products, especially when paired with creator affiliates. It also adds operational work: listings, fulfilment standards, creator samples and commission management. Treat it as its own channel with a plan and budget, and judge it on profit after commissions and fees, not just gross sales.

### How should I split my budget between Meta and TikTok?
Keep most spend on the channel that is already profitable and ring-fence a fixed test budget for the new one, such as 10% to 20% of total spend for a set window. Increase TikTok spend only if total revenue keeps pace. That is a planning rule of thumb, not a benchmark.

# Facebook Ads vs Google Ads for Ecommerce: How They Work Together
URL: https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/compare/meta-ads-vs-google-ads
Summary: Facebook ads vs Google ads for ecommerce: demand creation vs capture, Shopping and PMax, creative, attribution overlap and how to budget for both.

[Home](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/) / [Services](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/services) / Meta vs Google

        By [Gaurav Kapoor](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/about), Founder, Brand Scaling · Updated 2026-11-05

        The facebook ads vs google ads for ecommerce debate often treats them as rivals. In practice they sit at different points of the buying journey. Meta puts your product in front of people who did not know it existed. Google catches people who are already typing a product or brand name into a search bar.
This guide explains how each works for an online store, where Shopping and [Performance Max](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/google-shopping-ads-agency) fit, how creative differs, why the two platforms double-count sales, and how to budget for both without fooling yourself.

        
## Are Facebook ads or Google ads better for ecommerce?
They do different jobs. Facebook and Instagram ads create demand by showing products to people who were not searching. Google Shopping and search capture demand from people already looking. Most growing DTC brands use Meta as the main acquisition engine and Google to capture branded and product searches, then judge both on blended results.

        
        
        
          
## Facebook ads vs Google ads at a glance

          A general comparison of how the platforms behave for a typical Shopify brand. It is not a statistic about either channel.

          
          FactorMeta (Facebook and Instagram)Google (Search, Shopping, PMax)Primary roleDemand creationDemand captureHow people find youAds in feeds, Stories and ReelsSearch results, Shopping listings, YouTube, DisplayMain leverCreative and offerProduct feed, keywords, bids and search volumeScale ceilingGrows with creative and budgetLimited by how many people searchCreative needsHigh volume of new video and static adsClean feed images and titles, some video for PMaxBest forNew products, new categories, impulse purchasesKnown products, branded search, high-intent buyersAttribution riskUndercounts sales that finish on searchClaims credit for demand Meta created
          
          
        
          
## Demand creation vs demand capture

          Meta is a discovery platform. It finds likely buyers from behaviour and purchase signals and shows them an ad they did not ask for. If the creative and offer are strong, Meta can scale a brand that nobody is searching for yet. That is why most DTC growth stories start on Meta.
Google works the other way. Someone searches for a product, a problem or your brand name, and Google shows ads that match. Intent is high, so conversion rates on branded and product searches are often strong, but volume is capped by how many people search. If nobody has heard of your product, there is little search demand to capture.
The two feed each other. Meta ads make people curious, many of them later search your brand or product name, and Google catches that search. Cut Meta and branded search often falls a few weeks later.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## Google Shopping and Performance Max for online stores

          For ecommerce, the core Google formats are Shopping ads, which show product images, prices and your store name, and Performance Max, which uses your product feed and assets across Search, Shopping, YouTube, Display and Gmail in one campaign.

          - Your product feed is the foundation: accurate titles, clean images, correct prices and stock status matter more than clever bids.
- Separate branded search from non-branded so Performance Max does not take credit for people who would have found you anyway.
- Feed titles should lead with the words people search, such as product type, key feature and size.
- Give PMax real creative assets, including short videos, or Google will generate weaker ones automatically.
- Review search terms and product performance regularly and exclude what does not pay back.

          
          
          
        
          
## Creative: where the work goes

          On Meta, creative is the main lever. The algorithm handles targeting; your job is to give it enough new angles, hooks and formats to find buyers. That is why we produce 30 to 50+ new ad creatives and angles a month for partner brands.
On Google, the feed does most of the work in Shopping, and copy matters more than visuals in Search. Performance Max needs images, headlines and video, but the volume required is far lower than on Meta. The skill shifts from creative production to feed management, keyword control and bid strategy.
That difference matters when you staff the channels. A great Meta buyer is not automatically a great Google Shopping manager, and the reverse is also true.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## Attribution overlap: why the numbers add up to more than 100%

          Each platform reports conversions using its own rules. A customer might see a Meta ad on Monday, search your brand on Thursday and click a Shopping ad before buying. Meta counts that sale under its [attribution window](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/attribution-window). Google counts it too. Add the two dashboards together and you have more revenue than Shopify recorded.
That is why the most reliable check is blended: total store revenue divided by total ad spend across all channels ([MER](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/mer)), and new customers acquired against total spend. Use platform ROAS to optimize inside each platform, and blended numbers to decide how much to give each one.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## How to budget for both

          A practical approach for most DTC brands is to treat Meta as the growth budget and Google as the capture budget. Fund branded search and core Shopping campaigns so you do not lose high-intent buyers to competitors, then put most incremental spend where new demand is created.

          - Start Google with branded search and Shopping on your best sellers.
- Keep the majority of growth spend on Meta while it scales profitably.
- Increase Google spend when non-branded search and Shopping hold their own on blended results.
- Test a pause or reduction on one channel and watch total revenue, not just its dashboard.
- Check your [break-even ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tools/break-even-roas-calculator) so both channels have a clear profitability floor.

          
          
          
        
          
## Which to prioritise for your product

          The right balance depends heavily on whether people already search for what you sell. A quick way to check is to look at search suggestions and Google Shopping results for your product type. If you see plenty of competing listings, there is demand to capture. If you see almost nothing, you will have to create that demand first, and that is a job for Meta.

          - New or unusual products that solve a problem people do not search for: lead with Meta.
- Everyday categories with clear search terms, such as replacement parts or staples: Google Shopping can carry more weight early.
- Impulse and visual products such as fashion, beauty and gadgets: Meta first, Google to catch the brand searches it creates.
- Established brands with strong name recognition: protect branded search on Google and use Meta to keep growing new customer volume.

          
          
          
        
        
## Real results from client accounts
- [Supplement Case Study: $137,620 in One Month at 3.89x ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/record-breaking-month-generating-137620-25-revenue-roas-3): $137,620 / month, 3.89x ROAS
- [Jewelry Case Study: $54K in 7 Days at 4.43x ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/drove-54k-7-days-using-manual-bidding-campaigns-jewelry): $54K in 7 days, 4.43x ROAS
- [Dropshipping Case Study: $2.3M at 11.6x ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/finally-built-million-dollar-brand-2022-ending-2-3): $2.3M, 11.6x ROAS
- [Dropshipping Case Study: $491,798 in One Month](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/dropshipping-isn-get-rich-quick-scheme-it-path-building): $491,798 / month, 34% margin

## From first call to scaling, step by step
- Brand Growth Audit call (Week 0): A 1-on-1 review of your ad account, creative, store and unit economics with Gaurav Kapoor. Free, and you keep the findings.
- Foundation (Days 1 to 14): Tracking and Conversions API fixes, offer and margin changes, product page fixes and the first creative brief.
- Test (Days 15 to 45): Weekly creative batches built on a hook and angle matrix, read against your break-even ROAS, not platform vanity numbers.
- Optimize and scale (Day 45 onward): Conversion rate and AOV work, then budget steps of 20% to 30% on proven ads while MER and new-customer CAC hold.

        
## Proof from real accounts
- $137,620 Month at 3.89x ROAS: Supplement brand on Meta ([see the proof](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/record-breaking-month-generating-137620-25-revenue-roas-3))
- $54K In 7 days at 4.43x ROAS: Jewelry brand using manual bidding campaigns ([see the proof](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/drove-54k-7-days-using-manual-bidding-campaigns-jewelry))
- 30 to 50+ New ad creatives a month: Produced for partner brands ([see the proof](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/viral-creatives))

        
## Frequently asked questions

### Should a new ecommerce store start with Facebook or Google ads?
If your product is new and few people search for it, start with Facebook and Instagram ads, because they create demand. If people already search for your product type, Google Shopping can bring high-intent buyers quickly. Many brands run a small branded search and Shopping campaign alongside Meta from early on.

### Is Google Shopping better than Performance Max?
Neither is always better. Standard Shopping gives more control over products and bids, while Performance Max reaches more Google placements with less manual work. Many stores use both, with PMax for broad reach and Shopping or search for tighter control. The quality of your product feed matters more than the campaign type.

### Why does my Facebook and Google revenue add up to more than Shopify?
Both platforms claim credit for the same orders. A customer who saw a Meta ad and later clicked a Google Shopping ad can be counted by both. Use each platform's numbers to optimize within it, and use blended MER, total revenue divided by total ad spend, to judge overall performance.

### How much should I spend on Google vs Facebook ads?
There is no fixed ratio. A common starting point is to fully fund branded search and core Shopping so you capture existing demand, then put most growth spend on Meta. Shift budget toward Google as non-branded campaigns prove profitable on blended results. Your margins and search volume decide the split.

### Do Facebook ads help Google ads perform better?
Often, yes. Meta ads make people aware of your brand, and some of them later search your brand or product name, which shows up as Google branded search and Shopping conversions. That is why pausing Meta can reduce Google results a few weeks later, even though Google reports no direct link.

# DTC Agency Alternatives: An Honest Guide to Your Options
URL: https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/compare/brand-scaling-hacks-alternatives
Summary: DTC agency alternatives compared honestly: freelancers, in-house teams, PPC specialists, full-service agencies, creative studios and consultants.

[Home](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/) / [Services](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/services) / Agency Alternatives

        By [Gaurav Kapoor](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/about), Founder, Brand Scaling · Updated 2026-11-05

        If you are researching dtc agency alternatives, you probably want to know whether a full growth agency like ours is the right call, or whether something lighter or more specialised would serve you better. That is a fair question, and the honest answer is that it depends on your stage, budget and bottleneck.
This guide walks through the six main types of help available to a DTC brand, what each is good and bad at, and who it suits. We have also included a section on when Brand Scaling is not the right fit, because a bad match helps nobody.

        
## What are the alternatives to hiring a DTC growth agency?
The main DTC agency alternatives are a freelance media buyer, an in-house team, a specialist PPC agency, a full-service growth agency, a creative-only studio, or a consultant or coaching program. Each fits a different budget, stage and level of internal skill. The right choice depends on what is actually holding your growth back.

        
        
        
          
## The six main alternatives compared

          These are categories, not specific companies. Quality varies widely inside each one, so use this as a map and then check references and results for any individual provider.

          
          OptionTypical strengthsTypical weaknessesOften fitsFreelance media buyerLower cost, direct contact, flexibleSingle point of failure, limited creative and CROEarly brands with modest spendIn-house teamFull focus, deep brand knowledge, controlHighest fixed cost, slow to hire, skill gapsLarge, stable spend with internal leadershipSpecialist PPC agencyDeep skill on one channel such as GoogleNarrow view, may not handle creative or retentionBrands with one clear channel needFull-service growth agencyBuying, creative, CRO, email under one planHigher fee, needs enough spend to justify itBrands with product-market fit ready to scaleCreative-only studioHigh volume of UGC and ad creativeDoes not run or optimize the adsBrands with a strong buyer who needs more creativeConsultant or coachingLowest cost, builds your own skillYou still do the work and the hoursFounders who want to run ads themselves
          
          
        
          
## Freelancers and in-house teams

          
          
          
          
### Freelance media buyer
A good freelancer can be excellent value. You get direct access to the person doing the work and usually a lower fee than an agency. The risks are capacity and coverage: if they get sick, take on too many clients or leave, your account stalls. Most freelancers focus on campaign management, so you will still need a source of creative, tracking help and store improvements.

### In-house team
Building your own team gives you full focus and keeps knowledge inside the business. It also carries the highest fixed cost and the slowest start, because hiring and onboarding take months. It tends to make sense once spend is large and stable, and once someone senior can manage the team. Our agency vs in-house comparison breaks down the cost arithmetic in detail.

          
        
          
## Specialist agencies and full-service growth agencies

          
          
          
          
### Specialist PPC agency
Channel specialists, for example a [Google Shopping](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/google-shopping-ads-agency) or Amazon-focused agency, often have deeper expertise in that one channel than a generalist. That is valuable if your growth really depends on that channel. The trade-off is a narrow view: they may optimize their channel well while the bigger constraint sits in your creative, offer, landing page or retention.

### Full-service growth agency
This is the category Brand Scaling sits in. One team handles paid media, [creative strategy](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/creative-strategy-agency) and production, tracking, store conversion and retention flows under a single plan. The benefit is that the pieces are joined up: the ads, the product page and the email flows are built to work together. The cost is a higher fee, which only makes sense once you are spending enough on ads for improvements to pay back.

          
        
          
## Creative studios and consultants

          
          
          
          
### Creative-only studio
If you already have a strong media buyer and your bottleneck is creative volume, a creative studio can be the most efficient fix. Studios produce [UGC](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/viral-creatives), edited video and statics at scale. Our sister studio, SevenFigureStudio, does exactly this for UGC video ads. The limitation is that a studio does not run the ads, read the data or decide what to test next.

### Consultant or coaching program
Consultants and coaching programs teach you or your team to run the work. They cost the least and build lasting skill, which suits founders who enjoy the ad account and have the time. The catch is that you still do the execution. If your time is better spent on product, operations or partnerships, coaching can become an expensive way to stay busy.

          
        
          
## When Brand Scaling is not the right fit

          We work best with DTC brands that already have product-market fit, typically doing about $20K to $2M+ a month and spending at least $10K to $20K a month on paid ads. Outside that range, one of the alternatives above is often a better use of your money.

          - You are pre-launch or have not yet made consistent sales: a consultant or freelancer is usually a better first step.
- Your ad budget is very small: our fees would take too large a share of spend to pay back.
- You only need ad creative and already have a strong buyer: a creative studio is more efficient.
- You only need one channel managed, such as Amazon: a channel specialist will go deeper.
- You want to learn to run ads yourself: coaching builds your skill more directly.
- You need guaranteed results by a fixed date: no honest agency can promise that.

          
          
          
        
          
## How to choose between them

          Start with the bottleneck, not the option. If your ads convert but you cannot produce new creative fast enough, the fix is creative. If traffic converts poorly, the fix is the store. If nothing is joined up, you probably need a team that owns the full plan.
Whoever you consider, ask for published results in brands like yours, a clear process and timeline, who exactly will work on your account, and confirmation that you keep ownership of your ad accounts and data. Compare pricing models carefully: retainers, percentage of spend and performance fees shift risk in different ways.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is a freelancer or an agency better for a DTC brand?
A freelancer is often better value for early brands with modest spend that mainly need campaigns managed. An agency usually fits better once you need creative production, tracking, CRO and retention handled together, and when relying on one person becomes a risk. Judge both on published results in brands similar to yours.

### What is the cheapest alternative to a DTC agency?
Consulting or coaching is usually the lowest cash cost, because you do the execution yourself. The real cost is your time. A freelancer is the next step up. Compare options on total cost, including your hours and any creative you must buy separately, rather than on the fee alone.

### When should I not hire a growth agency?
Hold off if you have not yet found consistent sales, your ad budget is very small, or your only gap is one narrow task such as creative volume. In those cases a consultant, freelancer or creative studio usually gives a better return. A growth agency pays back best once there is something proven to scale.

### Do I need separate agencies for ads and creative?
Not necessarily. Some brands pair a media buyer with a creative studio, which works well when communication is tight. Others prefer one team that owns both, so testing plans and creative briefs come from the same data. The split approach needs someone on your side to coordinate the two.

### What should I ask any agency or freelancer before hiring?
Ask for results in brands like yours, a clear process with timelines, who will actually run your account, how much new creative they produce each month, how they report blended results, what the fee includes, and whether you keep full ownership of your ad accounts, pixel and data.
