# Average Ecommerce ROAS: What Our Published Case Studies Show
URL: https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/benchmarks/ecommerce-roas
Summary: Average ecommerce ROAS from our 25 published case studies: median 3.97x, ranges by niche, and an honest note on why this sample is biased.

[Home](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/) / [Benchmarks](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/benchmarks) / ROAS Benchmark

        By [Gaurav Kapoor](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/about), Founder, Brand Scaling · Updated 2026-11-12

        Searching for the average ecommerce ROAS usually turns up a single number with no source. We would rather show you exactly where our numbers come from and what they cannot tell you.
This page is built only from the ROAS figures stated in the client results we have published on this site. That makes it transparent, but also small and biased toward accounts that went well. Use it to sense-check your own results, alongside your [break-even ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tools/break-even-roas-calculator) and blended [MER](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/mer), not as a target you must hit.

        
## What is the average ecommerce ROAS in your case studies?
Across the 25 published Brand Scaling case studies that state a ROAS, the median is 3.97x and the middle half sits between 3.61x and 4.39x, with a full range of 2.06x to 11.6x. These are platform-reported figures from successful accounts, so treat them as a reference point, not an industry average.

        
        
        
          
## The headline numbers

          Of the [case studies](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/case-studies) published on this site, 25 state a ROAS figure. Taken together:

          - Median ROAS: 3.97x.
- Middle half of cases: 3.61x to 4.39x.
- Lowest published ROAS: 2.06x.
- Highest published ROAS: 11.6x.

          
          
### Why we use the median
One result at 11.6x would pull a simple average upwards and make the typical case look better than it is. The median, the middle value when all 25 are lined up, is less affected by outliers. The middle half shows where most of the published cases cluster.

          
        
          
## ROAS by niche in our published case studies

          The table groups the same 25 cases by niche. Some niches have only one or two cases, so a range here describes our published results, not what every brand in that category achieves.

          - Dropshipping has the widest range, from short high-volume pushes to the 11.6x year-long result.
- General DTC includes high-spend scaling periods, where ROAS often drops as spend rises.
- Jewelry is a single case and should not be read as a niche benchmark.

          NicheCases with a stated ROASPublished ROAS rangeSupplements43.89x to 4.51xFashion43.56x to 5.49xFitness33.61x to 4.37xSkincare23.64x to 4.39xDropshipping72.53x to 11.6xGeneral DTC42.06x to 3.8xJewelry14.43x
          
          
        
          
## Methodology and limitations

          We want this to be useful, which means being clear about what it is and is not.

          - Source: the ROAS stated in client result posts published on this site, nothing else.
- Platform-reported: figures are the ROAS shown by the ad platform, mostly Meta, not blended store-level results.
- Not a random sample: we published these results because they were worth sharing.
- Skews to successful accounts: weaker months and accounts that did not work out are under-represented.
- Small samples per niche: one to seven cases per niche is not enough to call it a category average.
- Different time windows: some results cover a single day, others a month or a full year.

          
          
### What that means for you
Read these numbers as what success has looked like in our published work, not as the average ecommerce ROAS across all stores. Many profitable brands run below 3.6x, and some accounts need a lower ROAS to grow new customer volume. Your own margins decide what is good.

          
        
          
## How to compare your own ROAS

          Before comparing yourself with any benchmark, work out your break-even ROAS. It is the ROAS at which ad spend exactly uses up your gross profit, and it comes from your margin, not from anyone else's results.
Break-even ROAS = 1 / [contribution margin](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/contribution-margin) before ad spend. For example, if a $100 order leaves $40 after product cost, shipping, payment fees and discounts, your margin is 40% and your break-even ROAS is 1 / 0.40 = 2.5x. At 2.5x you make no profit on that order; above it you do. A brand with a 60% margin breaks even at about 1.67x, so a 3x ROAS means something very different for each.
Then check blended MER: total store revenue divided by total marketing spend across every channel. MER shows whether your overall ad spend is paying back, regardless of which platform claims the sale.

          - Calculate break-even ROAS from your real contribution margin.
- Compare platform ROAS with that floor, not with someone else's figure.
- Track blended MER weekly to see the true return on total spend.
- Compare like with like: the same time window, attribution setting and season.

          
          
          
        
          
## What moves ROAS up or down in our published cases

          Looking across the published results, a few patterns explain much of the spread between the low and high ends of the range. None of them is a rule, but they help you read any ROAS figure in context.
Time window matters. A single strong day or week can show a higher or lower ROAS than a full month, because short windows capture spikes such as a launch, a sale or a viral creative. Spend level matters too. The lowest figures in our general DTC group come from heavy scaling periods, where the goal was more revenue and more new customers rather than the highest possible ratio. Seasonality plays a part: several cases come from Q4 and [BFCM](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/blog/bfcm-meta-ads-playbook), when demand is high but auction costs rise as well.
Finally, the offer and the product page set the ceiling. The same ads sent to a faster, clearer product page with a stronger bundle can lift ROAS without touching the ad account at all.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## Why platform ROAS and blended ROAS differ

          Platform ROAS is what Meta, TikTok or Google report inside their own dashboards. Each platform counts a sale if someone clicked or viewed an ad within its [attribution window](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/attribution-window), using its own model. Several platforms can claim the same order, and some sales are missed entirely when tracking is blocked or incomplete.
[Blended ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/blended-roas), often called MER, ignores who claims what. It divides total revenue by total ad spend. It includes repeat customers, organic sales and email revenue, and it is not inflated by double counting. It is less precise for deciding which ad to scale, but more honest about whether the business is making money.
Use platform ROAS to make decisions inside a platform, such as which creative or audience to scale. Use blended MER and new customer cost to decide total budget.

          
          
          
          
        
        
## Real results from client accounts
- [Dropshipping Case Study: $2.3M at 11.6x ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/finally-built-million-dollar-brand-2022-ending-2-3): $2.3M, 11.6x ROAS
- [Skincare Case Study: $115,416 in 20 Days at 4.39x ROAS on $26,271 Ad Spend](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/26271-spent-115416-generated-4-39-roas-skincare-brand-crushed-it): $115,416 in 20 days, 4.39x ROAS
- [DTC Ecommerce Case Study: $374,103 in 16 Days at 2.82x ROAS on $132,832 Ad Spend](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/new-dtc-client-results-last-16-days-132832-ad-spend-374103): $374,103 in 16 days, 2.82x ROAS
- [Dropshipping Case Study: $491,798 in One Month](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/dropshipping-isn-get-rich-quick-scheme-it-path-building): $491,798 / month, 34% margin

## Frequently asked questions

### What is a good ROAS for an ecommerce store?
[A good ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/blog/good-roas-for-ecommerce) is any figure comfortably above your break-even ROAS, which you calculate as 1 divided by your contribution margin before ad spend. A brand with a 40% margin breaks even at 2.5x. In our published cases the median is 3.97x, but those are success-biased examples, not a universal target.

### Is a 4x ROAS good for ecommerce?
For many DTC brands with healthy margins, 4x platform ROAS is profitable, and it sits close to the 3.97x median in our published cases. Whether it is good for you depends on your margins, your repeat purchase rate and whether blended MER confirms what the platform reports. Always check against your break-even first.

### Why is my ROAS lower than these case studies?
These are published wins, mostly platform-reported, from accounts we chose to share. They skew toward strong results, and some cover single days or short pushes. Your ROAS may also differ because of margins, price point, attribution settings or a focus on new customers. Compare against your own break-even ROAS instead.

### Does ROAS go down as you scale ad spend?
Often, yes. As spend rises, the platform reaches beyond your most responsive buyers, so ROAS can fall even while total profit grows. Our published high-spend result of $374,103 on $132,832 spend ran at 2.82x. The question is whether total contribution profit rises, not whether ROAS stays fixed.

### What is the difference between ROAS and MER?
ROAS usually means platform-reported revenue divided by spend on that platform. MER, or blended ROAS, divides total store revenue by total marketing spend across all channels. ROAS helps you optimize within a platform. MER shows whether your total ad spend is paying back, and it avoids double counting between platforms.

### How was this ROAS benchmark calculated?
We took every case study published on this site that states a ROAS figure, 25 in total, and calculated the median, the middle half and the full range, then grouped them by niche. The figures are platform-reported, not a random sample, and skew toward successful accounts.

# Break Even ROAS Calculator
URL: https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tools/break-even-roas-calculator
Summary: Free break even ROAS calculator for ecommerce. Enter price, COGS, shipping and fees to get your break-even ROAS, CPA and contribution margin per order.

[Home](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/) / [Free Tools](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tools) / Free Ecommerce Tool

        By [Gaurav Kapoor](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/about), Founder, Brand Scaling · Updated 2026-11-05

        This break even [ROAS calculator](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/roas-calculator) tells you the lowest [return on ad spend](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/blog/what-is-roas) your store can accept before every order starts losing money. Enter four numbers from your Shopify admin and supplier invoices, and it returns your [contribution margin](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/contribution-margin) per order, your margin as a percentage, the break-even ROAS and the break-even CPA.
Most founders judge Meta or TikTok results against a ROAS number someone else told them was good. That number means nothing until you know your own floor. A brand with cheap COGS can be profitable at 1.6x, while a brand with heavy shipping costs can lose money at 2.5x. Work out the floor first, then set targets above it.

        
## What is break-even ROAS?
Break-even ROAS is the return on ad spend at which an order covers its product cost, shipping, payment fees and the ad spend that produced it, leaving zero profit. Divide selling price by contribution margin per order before ads. A $60 order with $32.20 of margin breaks even at 1.86x ROAS.

        
        
## Break-even ROAS calculator
Inputs: Selling price per order ($), Product cost (COGS) per order ($), Shipping and fulfilment per order ($), Payment processing fee (%). The calculator runs in your browser; nothing is stored.

        
          
## How to use the break-even ROAS calculator

          Use per-order figures, not monthly totals. If your average order contains more than one unit, use the [average order value](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/aov) and the average landed cost of a typical basket.

          - Selling price per order: what the customer pays for the products, after discounts. Use your average order value net of discount codes if most orders use one.
- Product cost (COGS) per order: the landed cost of the goods, including the supplier price, inbound freight and duties.
- Shipping and fulfilment per order: outbound postage, pick and pack fees, packaging and any 3PL charges you pay on each order.
- Payment processing fee %: the percentage your payment provider takes from each order. Enter the percentage only; small fixed per-transaction fees can be added to the shipping line.

          
          
          
        
          
## The break-even ROAS formula with a worked example

          The calculator first finds how much each order contributes before any ad spend, then works out how much revenue each ad dollar has to bring back to cover that margin exactly.
Contribution margin per order = price - COGS - shipping - (price x fee %)
Contribution margin % = contribution margin per order / price
Break-even ROAS = price / contribution margin per order, which is the same as 1 / contribution margin %
Break-even CPA = contribution margin per order
Example: a [skincare brand](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/case-studies/skincare-beauty) sells a $60 order. COGS is $18, shipping and fulfilment is $8 and the payment fee is 3%, which is $1.80 on a $60 order. Contribution margin per order is $60 - $18 - $8 - $1.80 = $32.20. That is a 53.7% contribution margin. Break-even ROAS is $60 / $32.20 = 1.86x, and the break-even CPA is $32.20. If Meta delivers a purchase for less than $32.20, that order made money.

          
          LineExample valueSelling price per order$60.00COGS per order$18.00Shipping and fulfilment$8.00Payment fee (3%)$1.80Contribution margin per order$32.20 (53.7%)Break-even ROAS1.86xBreak-even CPA$32.20
          
          
        
          
## How to read the result

          Your break-even ROAS is a floor, not a goal. Running exactly at that number means ads are paying for themselves but nothing is left for salaries, software, returns or profit. Most brands set a target ROAS comfortably above break-even for prospecting and accept something closer to break-even on campaigns that bring in new customers who are likely to reorder.
The break-even CPA is often more useful day to day than the ROAS figure, because it maps directly to the cost per purchase column in Ads Manager. When a campaign's CPA sits under your break-even CPA, it is contributing profit on the first order. To understand where the margin itself comes from, read our guide to contribution margin at /glossary/contribution-margin.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## What to do next

          If your break-even ROAS is above roughly 2.5x, the problem is usually the offer and unit economics rather than the ads. A higher price, a bundle that lifts order value, or cheaper fulfilment lowers the floor for every campaign you run.

          - Compare your actual Meta ROAS with the floor, using the standard ROAS calculator at /roas-calculator.
- Raise order value with bundles and test the effect in the AOV calculator at /tools/aov-calculator.
- Book a [Meta ads audit](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/meta-ads-audit) at /meta-ads-audit if campaigns sit below break-even and you cannot see why.

          
          
          
        
          
## Common mistakes

          Break-even ROAS is only as accurate as the costs you feed it. The errors below all push the number in the same direction, making the floor look lower and campaigns look safer than they are.

          - Using the product price instead of the net order value after discount codes, which makes the floor look lower than it is.
- Leaving out shipping you subsidise with free delivery. If you pay it, it belongs in the calculation.
- Ignoring returns and refunds. If a meaningful share of orders come back, reduce the selling price input to reflect net revenue kept.
- Judging break-even against platform-reported ROAS only, which can over-count conversions. Check blended numbers too.

          
          
          
        
        
        
## Proof from real accounts
- $50M+ Meta ad spend managed: Across our client accounts over 12+ years in ecommerce
- 56% Profit margin: $185,936 in 21 days for a dropshipping store ([see the proof](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/185936-21-days-56-profit-margin-scaled-dropshipping-store-beyond))
- 4.39x ROAS: $115,416 on $26,271 spend for a skincare brand ([see the proof](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/26271-spent-115416-generated-4-39-roas-skincare-brand-crushed-it))

        
## Frequently asked questions

### How do I calculate break-even ROAS?
Subtract product cost, shipping and payment fees from the selling price to get contribution margin per order. Then divide the selling price by that margin. A $60 order with $32.20 of margin has a break-even ROAS of 1.86x. Below that number, each ad-driven order loses money; above it, the order contributes profit.

### Is break-even ROAS the same as target ROAS?
No. Break-even ROAS is the point where an order makes zero profit after ad spend. Target ROAS is the number you aim for, set above break-even so there is room for overheads, returns and profit. Many brands accept a lower target on new-customer campaigns if repeat purchases are strong.

### Should I include fixed costs like salaries in break-even ROAS?
Not in this calculation. Break-even ROAS uses variable costs that scale with each order: COGS, shipping and payment fees. Fixed costs such as salaries, software and rent are covered by the profit you earn above break-even. Mixing them in makes the number move every time volume changes.

### What is break-even CPA?
Break-even CPA is the most you can pay in ad spend to acquire one order without losing money on it. It equals your contribution margin per order before ads. If your margin is $32.20, any purchase that costs less than $32.20 in ad spend is profitable on the first order.

### How do I lower my break-even ROAS?
Improve contribution margin. You can raise prices, increase order value with bundles or upsells, negotiate lower product costs, reduce fulfilment fees or cut free shipping thresholds that erode margin. Each change lowers the ROAS your ads need to reach, which gives campaigns more room to scale before they hit the floor.

# TikTok Shop Break Even ROAS Calculator
URL: https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tools/tiktok-shop-break-even-roas-calculator
Summary: Free TikTok Shop break even ROAS calculator. Enter price, costs, referral fee and affiliate commission to see profit per order and your break-even ROAS.

[Home](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/) / [Free Tools](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tools) / Free Ecommerce Tool

        By [Gaurav Kapoor](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/about), Founder, Brand Scaling · Updated 2026-11-12

        This [TikTok Shop](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tiktok-shop-agency) [break even ROAS calculator](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tools/break-even-roas-calculator) shows what you keep from each order after TikTok and your creators take their share, and the lowest return your [TikTok ads](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tiktok-ads-agency) or [GMV Max](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/blog/tiktok-gmv-max) campaigns can run at without losing money. It also works as a TikTok Shop profit calculator and fees calculator: enter your price, product cost, shipping, referral fee and affiliate commission, and it returns profit per order before ads, total fees and commission, margin, break-even ROAS and the most you can pay in ads for one order.
TikTok Shop costs stack up faster than on your own Shopify store. The platform takes a referral fee on every sale, creators often take a commission on top, and ads come after both. Run the numbers per order first, then set your ad targets from the result.

        
## How do I calculate break-even ROAS for TikTok Shop?
Take your selling price and subtract product cost, shipping, the TikTok Shop referral fee and any affiliate commission. That is your profit per order before ads. Divide the price by it. A $35 order with $8 COGS, $6 shipping, an 8% example referral fee and 15% affiliate commission leaves $12.95, so break-even ROAS is 2.70x.

        
        
## TikTok Shop break-even ROAS calculator
Inputs: Selling price per order ($), Product cost (COGS) per order ($), Shipping and fulfilment you pay per order ($), TikTok Shop referral fee (example rate) (%), Affiliate commission you set (0 if none) (%), Other fee if charged separately (often 0) (%). The calculator runs in your browser; nothing is stored.

        
          
## How to use the TikTok Shop profit calculator

          Use per-order figures for a typical order, not monthly totals. Fees and commission are calculated as a percentage of the selling price, so the calculator adds them up for you.
A note on the referral fee: TikTok Shop rates vary by region, category and date. TikTok's US Seller University fee table listed a 6% referral fee for most categories, in effect since April 1, 2024, with a few jewelry and pre-owned categories lower. Several seller guides published in 2026 report a rise to 8% for most US categories from August 2026, but we could not confirm that figure on an official TikTok page as of November 2026. The calculator uses 8% as an example rate. Check Seller Center for the rate on your category and enter that.

          - Selling price per order: what the customer pays for a typical order, before tax.
- Product cost (COGS) per order: the landed cost of the goods, including supplier price, inbound freight and duties.
- Shipping and fulfilment you pay: postage, packaging and any 3PL or pick and pack fees that come out of your pocket. If TikTok or the buyer covers shipping, enter only your share.
- TikTok Shop referral fee %: the platform fee for your category, taken from Seller Center.
- Affiliate commission %: the rate you set for creators in your affiliate plan. If only some orders come through creators, enter a blended rate. For example, 40% of orders at 15% commission is 6%.
- Other fee %: any payment or extra platform fee your region charges separately. Leave it at 0 if your Seller Center statement shows none.

          
          
          
        
          
## The formula with a worked example

          The calculator works out what one order leaves you before ads, then turns that into a ROAS floor.
Fees and commission = price x (referral % + affiliate % + other %)
Profit per order before ads = price - COGS - shipping - fees and commission
Break-even ROAS = price / profit per order before ads
Break-even CPA = profit per order before ads
Margin before ads = profit per order before ads / price
Example (illustrative numbers, not client data): a $35 order with $8 COGS and $6 shipping and fulfilment. At an 8% example referral fee, TikTok takes $2.80. A 15% affiliate commission costs $5.25. With no other fee, fees and commission total $8.05. Profit per order before ads is $35 - $8 - $6 - $8.05 = $12.95, a 37.0% margin. Break-even ROAS is $35 / $12.95 = 2.70x, and you can spend up to $12.95 in ads to win one order before you lose money.
The table keeps everything else the same and changes only the affiliate commission, to show how much each extra point of commission raises your ROAS floor.

          
          Affiliate commissionFees and commissionProfit before adsMarginBreak-even ROAS0%$2.80$18.2052.0%1.92x10%$6.30$14.7042.0%2.38x15%$8.05$12.9537.0%2.70x20%$9.80$11.2032.0%3.13x25%$11.55$9.4527.0%3.70x
          
          
        
          
## How to read the result

          Break-even ROAS is your floor, not your goal. If your GMV Max campaign or TikTok ads deliver a ROAS above it, each ad-driven order makes money before overheads. Below it, every order you buy with ads loses money, even if revenue looks strong in Seller Center. GMV Max asks for a ROI target, which is gross revenue divided by ad spend, so you can compare it directly with the break-even ROAS here.
Two things change the answer more than people expect. First, affiliate commission: an order that comes through a creator video you also boost pays both the commission and the ad cost, so include the commission when you set ad targets for those orders. If your ad-driven orders pay no commission, run the calculator with affiliate at 0 for your ad floor. Second, price: a low-priced product leaves little room once fixed costs like shipping are paid, which is why bundles often make TikTok Shop maths work.
If the calculator shows No margin, your fees, commission and costs already use up the whole price, and no ad result can fix that.

          
          
          
          
        
          
## What to do next

          Use the break-even ROAS as the minimum for your campaigns, then aim above it so there is profit left for overheads and returns, which this calculator does not include. For the full plan, read our TikTok Shop strategy guide at /blog/tiktok-shop-strategy.

          - Raise order value with bundles or multi-packs, which spreads shipping across more product.
- Set affiliate commission from your margin, not from what other sellers offer.
- Compare TikTok Shop unit economics with your own site using the break-even [ROAS calculator](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/roas-calculator) at /tools/break-even-roas-calculator and our TikTok Shop vs Shopify guide at /blog/tiktok-shop-vs-shopify.
- If you want the shop and creator programme run for you, see our TikTok Shop agency at /tiktok-shop-agency. For in-feed ads that send traffic to your own store, see our TikTok ads agency at /tiktok-ads-agency.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is a good break-even ROAS for TikTok Shop?
There is no single good number, because it depends on your price, costs, referral fee and affiliate commission. A lower break-even ROAS is better, because it gives your ads more room. In our example it is 2.70x. Work out your own figure with the calculator, then set your GMV Max ROI target above it.

### How much does TikTok Shop take per sale?
TikTok charges a referral fee as a percentage of each sale, and the rate depends on your region and category. TikTok's US fee table listed 6% for most categories from April 2024, and 2026 seller guides report 8% from August 2026, which we could not confirm officially. Seller Center shows the current rate for your category. Affiliate commission, if you use creators, is on top.

### Should I include affiliate commission in my break-even ROAS?
Include it for any order that pays both commission and ad cost, such as a boosted creator video. Leave it out for ad orders that pay no commission. If you are not sure, enter a blended rate based on the share of orders that come through creators.

### How is TikTok Shop break-even ROAS different from my Shopify break-even ROAS?
The formula is the same, price divided by profit per order before ads, but TikTok Shop adds a referral fee and often a creator commission. That usually means less profit per order and a higher break-even ROAS for the same product.

### What does break-even CPA mean on TikTok Shop?
It is the most you can spend on ads to win one order without losing money. It equals your profit per order before ads. In the example, that is $12.95. If your cost per purchase is higher than that, each ad-driven order loses money.

For a full profit model with price, product cost, fees and CAC together, use the original [ROAS calculator](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/roas-calculator); the tools below each answer one specific question.

        
## Which ecommerce numbers should a DTC brand calculate first?
Start with break-even ROAS, because it tells you the lowest return your ads can run at without losing money on each order. Then track MER for the whole business, CAC against first-order profit, and LTV to see how much a customer is worth over time. These free ecommerce calculators do each of these in seconds.

## Frequently asked questions

### Are these ecommerce calculators free?
Yes. Every calculator on this page is free, runs in your browser and does not ask for an email. Nothing you type is stored or sent anywhere. They are built from the same formulas we use when we audit an ad account, and each page explains the maths so you can rebuild it in a spreadsheet.

### Which calculator should I use before scaling Meta ads?
Use the [break-even ROAS calculator](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tools/break-even-roas-calculator) first, then the Meta ads budget calculator. Break-even ROAS tells you the floor your campaigns must stay above, and the budget calculator turns a revenue goal into the daily spend, target CPA and weekly purchases you need. Together they show whether a scaling plan is realistic.

### What is the difference between ROAS and MER?
ROAS measures revenue attributed to one channel or campaign divided by that channel's ad spend. [MER](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/mer) divides total store revenue by total marketing spend across every channel, so it does not depend on attribution. We manage campaigns on ROAS and judge the business on MER, because platform attribution often over or under counts.

### How accurate are the results?
The maths is exact, but the result is only as good as the inputs. Use real numbers from Shopify and your ad accounts for the last 30 to 90 days, include shipping, fees and returns in your costs, and re-run the calculators whenever prices, margins or your channel mix change.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is a good ROAS for an ecommerce brand?
It depends on your margin. [A good ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/blog/good-roas-for-ecommerce) is one comfortably above your [break-even ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tools/break-even-roas-calculator), which is 1 divided by your [contribution margin](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/contribution-margin) before ads. In our published case studies the median is 3.97x, but a brand with 70% margins can be very profitable at 2x while a 30% margin brand loses money below 3.3x.

### Why not use industry-wide benchmark reports?
Many reports mix brands of every size, margin and attribution setup, and some cannot be checked at all. We prefer a smaller set of numbers we can prove with screenshots. When you compare yourself with any benchmark, compare against your own break-even ROAS and [MER](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/mer) trend first.

### Will you publish CPM, conversion rate and CAC benchmarks?
Yes, once we have enough accounts measured the same way to publish them honestly. Until then, use the free conversion rate, CAC and Meta ads budget calculators to work from your own data, which is more useful for decisions than any average.

# What Is ROAS? The ROAS Formula, Meaning and Examples
URL: https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/blog/what-is-roas
Summary: What is ROAS? The ROAS formula, worked examples, how to find your break-even ROAS and how ROAS differs from ROI and MER for ecommerce brands.

Direct Answer: ROAS (return on ad spend) is the revenue your ads generate for every dollar spent on them. The ROAS formula is revenue attributed to ads divided by ad spend: $20,000 in sales from $5,000 of ads is a 4x ROAS. Whether 4x is profitable depends on your margin, which sets your break-even ROAS.

      
      ROAS (Return On Ad Spend): Revenue attributed to advertising divided by the cost of that advertising, written as a ratio (4x or 4:1) or a percentage (400%). It measures revenue efficiency, not profit.

      
        
## The ROAS formula: how to calculate ROAS

        ROAS = revenue attributed to ads / ad spend.
Take the revenue your ad platform (or your analytics) credits to a campaign, and divide it by what you spent on that campaign over the same dates. If a Meta campaign spends $5,000 in a month and is credited with $20,000 of Shopify orders, ROAS = $20,000 / $5,000 = 4.0, usually written 4x, 4:1 or 400%.
Three rules keep the number honest: use the same date range for spend and revenue, use the same attribution setting every time you compare (for example 7-day click, 1-day view on Meta), and use revenue after discounts but before tax and shipping charged to the customer.

        
        Ad spendAttributed revenueROASAs a percentage$1,000$2,0002.0x200%$5,000$20,0004.0x400%$40,124$146,1843.64x364% (real skincare account, 27 days)$28,391$112,8663.98x398% (real early-BFCM result, 13 days)
        
### ROAS as a percentage, and converting ACoS to ROAS
ROAS as a percentage is the same number times 100: 3.5x is 350%. Amazon reports the inverse, ACoS (advertising cost of sale = ad spend / ad revenue). To convert, divide 1 by ACoS: an ACoS of 25% is a ROAS of 1 / 0.25 = 4x, and a 5x ROAS is an ACoS of 20%.

### Mistakes that make ROAS look better than it is
- Comparing a 7-day-click ROAS this month with a 1-day-click ROAS last month.
- Counting revenue that includes tax and shipping fees.
- Adding up ROAS from Meta, TikTok and Google: each platform credits itself, so the same order is often counted more than once.
- Judging [retargeting](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/blog/retargeting-for-dtc-brands) and prospecting together: retargeting looks high because many of those buyers would have purchased anyway.

      
        
## ROAS meaning: what the number tells you

        ROAS stands for return on ad spend. As a marketing term it answers one question: for every dollar spent on ads, how many dollars of revenue came back?
It measures revenue, not profit. A 4x ROAS means $4 of sales for every $1 of ads, before product cost, shipping, payment fees and returns are taken out. That is why the same 4x can be very profitable for a store with 70 percent margins and lose money for a store with 25 percent margins. ROAS is the right number for comparing ads and campaigns quickly; it is the wrong number for deciding whether the business is making money.

        
        
        
      
        
## Break-even ROAS: the number that matters

        [Break-even ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tools/break-even-roas-calculator) is the ROAS at which an order pays for its product, fulfilment and ad cost with nothing left over.
Break-even ROAS = 1 / [contribution margin](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/contribution-margin) %, where contribution margin is what is left of the order value after product cost (COGS), shipping and fulfilment, and payment fees.
Example: an $80 order with $24 product cost, $9 shipping and a 3 percent payment fee leaves $44.60, a 55.75 percent contribution margin. Break-even ROAS = 1 / 0.5575 = 1.79x. Below 1.79x that order loses money on ads; above it, the difference is profit. Work out your own with the break-even [ROAS calculator](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/roas-calculator) before setting any target.

        
        Contribution marginBreak-even ROAS70%1.43x60%1.67x50%2.0x40%2.5x30%3.33x
        
      
        
## ROAS vs ROI: what is the difference?

        ROAS compares revenue to ad spend only. ROI (return on investment) compares profit to every cost. A campaign can have a 3x ROAS and a negative ROI if product cost, shipping and fees take more than two thirds of the revenue.
Use ROAS to compare ads and campaigns day to day, because it is fast and every platform reports it. Use profit after ad spend (or ROI) to decide whether to keep scaling. The free ROAS calculator shows both: break-even ROAS and profit per order.

        
        
        
      
        
## ROAS vs MER: which should you scale on?

        Since iOS 14.5 and browser privacy changes, platform-reported ROAS misses some sales and double counts others. [MER](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/mer) (marketing efficiency ratio) avoids attribution entirely: total store revenue divided by total marketing spend across every channel.
Run campaigns on platform ROAS, because it is the only number available at ad level. Judge the business on MER and new-[customer acquisition cost](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/cac), because they match what actually lands in Shopify. If Meta ROAS dips but MER holds, the ads are usually still working and the purchases are being credited elsewhere.

        
        
        
      
        
## Gross ROAS vs net ROAS

        Gross ROAS is the number ad platforms report: total attributed revenue divided by ad spend, before anything is taken off. Net ROAS uses the revenue you actually keep, after refunds, returns, discounts, shipping charged and sales tax are removed.
The gap matters most for brands with high return rates or heavy discounting. If ads drive $40,000 in attributed sales on $10,000 of spend, gross ROAS is 4x. If $4,000 of those orders are refunded and $2,000 was tax and shipping, net revenue is $34,000 and net ROAS is 3.4x. Compare net ROAS, not gross, with your break-even ROAS, because break-even is calculated from margin on the money you keep.

        - ROAS tracking tools: Meta Ads Manager, [TikTok Ads](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tiktok-ads-agency) Manager and Google Ads report platform (gross) ROAS per campaign and ad.
- Shopify analytics shows net sales after returns and discounts, which you need for net ROAS and MER.
- Server-side tracking (Meta [Conversions API](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/conversions-api), TikTok Events API) recovers purchases that browser pixels miss.
- Attribution tools such as Triple Whale or Northbeam combine store and ad data in one view; a spreadsheet of daily Shopify net sales against total ad spend gives you MER for free.

        
        
      
        
## How to set a target ROAS

        Start from margin, not from someone else's benchmark. Work out break-even ROAS first, then decide how much profit each order must leave after ads.

        - Contribution margin 60%: break-even 1.67x; a target around 2.5x leaves room for profit.
- Contribution margin 50%: break-even 2.0x; target around 3x.
- Contribution margin 40%: break-even 2.5x; target 3.5x to 4x, or raise order value with bundles first.
- Subscription or high-repeat brands can accept a lower first-order target, because repeat purchases pay back the acquisition cost.

        
        
      
        
## How to improve ecommerce ROAS

        ROAS rises when either more revenue comes from the same spend or the same revenue costs less to buy. In practice the biggest levers are, in order:

        - Creative volume: test new hooks and angles every week so the best ad is always fresh. Our partner accounts launch 30 to 50+ new creatives a month.
- Order value: bundles, quantity breaks and post-purchase upsells lift revenue per order without extra ad spend.
- Conversion rate: a fast mobile product page that answers the main buying objection converts more of the traffic you already pay for.
- Account structure: fewer, broader campaigns (Advantage+ or broad targeting) exit the learning phase faster than many small, overlapping ad sets.
- Tracking: a working Conversions API means Meta optimises on real purchases, not on the share it can still see.

        
        
      
        
## What ROAS looks like in real accounts

        Across the 25 Brand Scaling [case studies](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/case-studies) that publish a ROAS, the median is 3.97x and the middle half sits between 3.61x and 4.39x. By niche: supplements 3.89x to 4.51x, fashion 3.56x to 5.49x, fitness 3.61x to 4.37x, skincare 3.64x to 4.39x. These are accounts that scaled well enough to publish, so treat them as what good looks like, not as an average.
For the full breakdown by niche, see the ecommerce [ROAS benchmarks](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/benchmarks/ecommerce-roas); for how to judge your own number against your margin, see [what a good ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/blog/good-roas-for-ecommerce) is for ecommerce.

        
        
        
      
      
## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is the ROAS formula?
ROAS equals revenue attributed to ads divided by ad spend over the same period. If a campaign spends $5,000 and is credited with $20,000 in sales, ROAS is $20,000 / $5,000 = 4x, also written 4:1 or 400%. Use the same date range and the same attribution setting whenever you compare two ROAS numbers.

### What does ROAS mean in marketing?
ROAS means return on ad spend: the revenue your advertising brings in for every dollar it costs. A 3x ROAS means $3 of sales per $1 of ads. It is a revenue measure, not a profit measure, so it has to be read against your margins and break-even ROAS before you can tell whether ads are making money.

### How do I calculate break-even ROAS?
Divide 1 by your contribution margin, which is what remains of the order value after product cost, shipping and payment fees. With a 55.75 percent contribution margin, break-even ROAS is 1 / 0.5575 = 1.79x. Any ROAS below that loses money on each ad-driven order; anything above it is profit before overheads.

### How do you convert ACoS to ROAS?
ROAS is the inverse of ACoS. Divide 1 by ACoS written as a decimal: an ACoS of 25 percent is 1 / 0.25 = 4x ROAS, and 20 percent ACoS is 5x ROAS. To go the other way, divide 1 by ROAS: a 2.5x ROAS equals a 40 percent ACoS, the metric Amazon advertising reports by default.

### Is a higher ROAS always better?
No. Very high ROAS often means spend is limited to retargeting and people who would have bought anyway. Growing brands deliberately accept a lower ROAS on prospecting to reach new customers, as long as it stays above break-even and blended MER holds. Total profit dollars matter more than the highest possible ratio.

### What is the difference between ROAS and ROI?
ROAS compares revenue to ad spend only. ROI compares profit to all costs, including product, shipping, fees and overheads. A campaign can show a healthy 3x ROAS and still have a negative ROI if those costs take more than two thirds of revenue, which is why margins have to be checked first.

# What Is a Performance Marketing Agency? DTC Growth Blueprint &amp; ROAS Framework
URL: https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/blog/performance-marketing-agency
Summary: What does an ecommerce performance marketing agency do? How DTC agencies scale Shopify brands with Meta and TikTok ads, CRO, creative testing and profit ROAS.

Direct Answer: A performance marketing agency is a growth firm that drives direct, trackable commercial outcomes, such as verified revenue, ROAS, customer acquisition, and qualified leads, rather than abstract vanity metrics like impressions or follower counts. In modern DTC ecommerce, high tier performance agencies combine algorithmic media buying across Meta and TikTok with in house direct response creative production and Shopify conversion rate optimization.

      
      Performance Marketing Agency: A specialized digital agency where client compensation, strategy, and daily campaign execution are directly anchored to measurable financial results (ROAS, CPA, MER, Net Margin).

      
        
## What does a performance marketing agency actually do?

        Unlike traditional branding agencies that focus on awareness campaigns, billboards, and social media aesthetic grids, a performance marketing agency is engineered around one singular objective: predictable, profitable customer acquisition.
Every dollar invested into paid ad channels (Meta, TikTok, Google Search, and YouTube) is mapped directly to conversions, [customer acquisition cost](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/cac) (CPA), and net [contribution margin](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/contribution-margin).
At Brand Scaling, managing over $50M in paid advertising across 150+ Shopify stores has proven that media buying alone no longer scales brands. Modern performance marketing is a tightly integrated triad:
1. [Direct Response Creative](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/viral-creatives) Engineering: Scripting, shooting, and editing 15 to 30 vertical video variations monthly.
2. Algorithmic Media Buying: Deploying broad targeting Advantage+ architectures with strict bid controls.
3. Full Funnel Conversion Optimization: Engineering landing pages, bundle upsells, and sub 1s load times.

        
        
        
      
        
## What is DTC performance marketing?

        DTC performance marketing is paid advertising for direct-to-consumer brands that is judged only on what it sells. An ecommerce performance marketing agency is the team that runs it for you, paid to grow orders and profit rather than reach. Every campaign on Meta, TikTok or Google is measured on orders, revenue, cost per new customer and profit after ad spend, not on reach or awareness.
It differs from performance marketing for lead generation or apps in three ways. The product is bought on the spot, often from a single video, so creative carries most of the work. The store is part of the funnel, so product page speed, the offer and checkout decide how much of the paid traffic converts. And margins are thin enough that the same ROAS can be profitable for one brand and a loss for another, so targets start from unit economics rather than benchmarks.

        
        
        
      
        
## What an ecommerce ROAS improvement agency actually changes

        When an agency promises to [improve ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/blog/what-is-roas), ask what it will change, because ROAS only moves for a few reasons: more revenue from the same spend, or the same revenue for less spend. In practice the work falls into four areas.

        - Creative: new hooks and angles every week, so spend moves to fresh winners instead of fatigued ads.
- Account structure: fewer, broader campaigns with clear budget and bid rules, so the platform optimises on enough purchases.
- Store and offer: product page, bundles and post-purchase upsells, so each click is worth more.
- Measurement: [Conversions API](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/conversions-api) and blended [MER](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/mer), so you can see whether a higher platform ROAS is real or only a shift in attribution.

        
        
      
        
## How to find an ecommerce growth agency that specializes in scaling DTC brands

        An [ecommerce growth agency](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/) that specializes in DTC brands works only, or mostly, with brands that sell their own products online, and it can show published results from stores like yours. Generalist agencies that also serve SaaS, local businesses or lead generation tend to optimize for leads and clicks, not for orders and contribution margin.
Use five checks before you sign. They apply whether you are hiring for Meta, TikTok or a [Google Ads agency](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/blog/choose-google-ads-agency-dtc).

        - Proof in your range: [case studies](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/case-studies) with spend, revenue and ROAS from brands at your monthly revenue, not only logos.
- Creative in-house: DTC scaling depends on new ads every week, so ask who writes, films and edits them.
- Profit-based targets: they should ask for your margins and set a [break-even ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tools/break-even-roas-calculator) before setting any target.
- Store work included: product page, offer and checkout changes, because paid traffic converts on your Shopify store.
- You own everything: ad accounts, pixel, data and creative stay in your name, and reporting shows blended MER, not platform ROAS alone.

        
        
      
        
## Traditional marketing agencies vs. performance agencies

        Understanding the distinction between traditional creative agencies and performance driven growth partners is critical for brand founders looking to scale beyond $100K/month:

        
        DimensionTraditional Creative AgencyPerformance Marketing AgencyPrimary KPIBrand awareness, impressions, reach, social engagementNet revenue, blended ROAS, CPA, and customer LTVCreative ApproachPolished, cinema style brand films produced over monthsRapid UGC, native TikTok hooks, and weekly iterative testingChannel MasteryBroad media placements, PR, and billboard takeoversAlgorithmic Meta Ads, TikTok Shop, Google PMax, and CAPIReporting CadenceMonthly slide decks with vanity metricsDaily live dashboards, blended MER tracking, and Slack commsAccountabilityPaid regardless of whether the campaign drives salesRetainers and scale incentives tied to performance targets
        
      
        
## The 4 pillars of modern DTC performance marketing

        High Converting Direct Response Video Creatives:
In modern Meta and TikTok advertising, creative is your targeting. Winning agencies do not rely on generic stock video; they analyze second by second drop off rates and engineer distinct hooks (problem agitation, founder origin, side by side comparison, social proof UGC). Explore our 58+ Vertical Video Ad Winners to see this in practice.
Full Funnel Shopify [Conversion Rate Optimization](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cro-agency) (CRO):
Scaling ad spend without optimizing on page conversion is like pouring water into a leaky bucket. Performance agencies optimize product display pages (PDPs), introduce 1 click bundle upsells, and streamline mobile checkout flows to maximize [Average Order Value](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/aov) (AOV).
Server Side Data Tracking & Conversions API (CAPI):
With browser tracking restrictions, resilient server to server tracking via Meta Conversions API and first party pixels is mandatory to feed high fidelity purchase signals back to advertising algorithms.
Mathematical Unit Economics & Profit Protection:
Scaling spend without understanding break even metrics leads to bankruptcy. Top performance teams model contribution margin, blended MER, and return on capital before scaling daily budgets.

        
        
        
      
        
## The metrics that matter: Beyond vanity ROAS

        A true performance partner monitors full funnel unit economics:
Blended MER (Marketing Efficiency Ratio): Total revenue divided by total marketing expenditure across all platforms.
Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC): The exact cost to acquire a first time purchasing customer.
Contribution Margin (CM): Net profit remaining after subtracting COGS, ad spend, shipping, and merchant processing fees.
First Time vs. Returning Customer Split: Ensuring that paid acquisition fuels sustainable long term business equity.

        
        
        
      
        
## How to vet and choose the right agency for your brand

        When hiring a performance marketing agency, ask these critical vetting questions:
1. Can I see live screen recordings of ad dashboards, not just screenshots? (Inspect our 150+ Verified Case Studies for real client dashboard recordings).
2. Do you produce the video creative in house, or do I have to provide the videos?
3. What is your strategy for creative fatigue once a winning ad stops performing?
4. How do you protect net profit margins when ad auction CPMs fluctuate?

        
        
        
      
        
## How to choose an ecommerce growth agency that specializes in scaling DTC brands

        Ecommerce growth agencies that specialize in scaling DTC brands look similar on their websites: the same platform logos, the same ROAS screenshots. The difference shows up in how the work is set up. A specialist runs creative, media buying, the store and retention as one system, because a DTC brand rarely stalls for a single reason. Spend stops scaling when creative fatigues, when the product page cannot convert colder traffic, or when first-order margin cannot cover the cost of a new customer.
So judge an agency on three things: who makes the ads and how many new ones launch each month, whether they will change the store and the offer rather than only the campaigns, and which number they report first. An agency that leads with blended MER and new-customer CAC is managing your business; one that leads with platform ROAS is managing a dashboard. Ask the questions below on the first call.

        
        
        
### Questions to ask before you sign
- Can you show live ad account or Shopify dashboards, not just logos and testimonials?
- Who produces the creative, and how many new ads a month will we launch?
- Will you touch the store (product pages, offers, checkout), or only the ads?
- Which number do you report first: platform ROAS or blended MER and new-customer CAC?
- Do we own the ad account, pixel, data and creative if we leave?
- What happens in the first 14 days?

### Red flags
- Guaranteed ROAS or revenue numbers before they have seen your account.
- Reporting that only shows platform ROAS and clicks.
- Ten ad sets of interest targeting and three creatives a month.
- Long contracts with no performance review points.

      
        
## DTC performance marketing: which channels do what

        Performance marketing for a DTC brand is not one channel. Each one has a different job, and a good agency budgets for the job, not for the channel.

        
        ChannelMain jobWhen it leadsMeta ads (Facebook, Instagram)Finding new customers at scale with creativeMost DTC brands from $20K to $2M+ a monthTikTok ads and TikTok ShopReach and creator-led discovery, in-app checkoutVisual, demo-friendly and impulse productsGoogle Search and ShoppingCapturing people already searchingBrands with search demand or a known categoryEmail and SMS (Klaviyo)Repeat purchases and lifetime valueEvery brand once traffic is flowingShopify CROTurning more paid traffic into ordersBefore scaling any paid channel
        
      
        
## What capabilities should a Google Ads agency have for DTC ecommerce?

        If Google is part of the mix, the agency should be able to: run a clean Merchant Center feed with optimised titles and images; separate brand search from non-brand so brand traffic does not inflate results; run Performance Max with audience signals from your customer lists; set target ROAS from your margins rather than a default; and report Google alongside Meta on blended MER so the two channels are not both claiming the same sale. For most DTC brands Google captures demand that Meta and TikTok create, so the agency should plan them together.

        
        
        
      
      
## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is a performance marketing agency?
A performance marketing agency is a specialized digital marketing partner that designs, executes, and scales paid ad campaigns where success is measured by trackable financial returns such as revenue, ROAS, and customer acquisition costs.

### How do performance marketing agencies charge?
Performance agencies typically operate on a base monthly management retainer plus a percentage of ad spend or a performance incentive based on net revenue scaled past an agreed baseline.

### What is the difference between digital marketing and performance marketing?
Digital marketing is an umbrella term covering all online activities, including SEO, organic social, and brand PR. Performance marketing is specifically focused on paid advertising and direct response conversions where every dollar is tracked against revenue generated.

### When should an ecommerce brand hire a performance marketing agency?
Brands should consider a performance agency when they have validated product market fit (typically $20k+/month in revenue) and need a repeatable, scalable creative and media buying engine to break through to $100k to $500k per month.

### Which agencies are best for scaling DTC ecommerce brands?
The best fit is an agency that runs creative, media buying and Shopify conversion work together, shows live dashboards as proof, and reports on blended MER and new-customer CAC rather than platform ROAS alone.

### What should I look for in an ecommerce growth agency?
Live account proof, in-house creative volume of 30 or more new ads a month, willingness to fix the store as well as the ads, full ownership of your accounts and data, and a clear plan for the first 14 days.

### What capabilities should a Google Ads agency have for DTC ecommerce?
A clean Merchant Center feed, brand and non-brand search separated, Performance Max with first-party audience signals, target ROAS set from your margins, and reporting on blended MER alongside Meta.

### Which Google Ads agencies are best for scaling DTC ecommerce brands?
The best Google Ads agencies for DTC brands run Shopping and Performance Max from a clean product feed, split branded from non-branded search, and judge results on new-customer revenue and blended MER rather than Google-reported ROAS. Ask for DTC case studies with spend and revenue at your size before choosing one.

### What does an ecommerce growth agency that specializes in DTC do differently?
It plans around orders and margin instead of leads: creative testing every week, account structures that give the algorithm enough purchases, store and offer changes that raise conversion rate and order value, and reporting on contribution margin and new-customer CAC.

# Facebook Ad Library (Meta Ads Library): How We Find Winning Ads and Scaled a DTC Brand to $376K in 25 Days
URL: https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/blog/meta-ads-library
Summary: How to use the free Facebook Ad Library (Meta Ads Library): find long-running competitor ads, turn them into tests, and how one brand hit $376K in 25 days.

Direct Answer: The Meta Ads Library is Meta's free, public database of every active ad on Facebook and Instagram. We use it to find competitor ads that have run for 2 weeks or more, because brands only keep paying for ads that make money. We study why those ads work, test our own versions at $20 per ad set, and move the winners into a CBO campaign. That process took a DTC skincare brand to $376,000 in revenue in 25 days.

      Watch the video: How We Scaled a DTC Brand to $376K in 25 Days With Meta Ads (Live Breakdown)

      
## Key takeaways
- An ad that has run for 2 weeks or more is a winner signal. Brands do not keep paying for losing ads.
- Your ad must make its point in 5 to 8 seconds. Longer explainer ads should stay under 30 to 40 seconds.
- Test at $20 per ad set, 7 to 10 ad sets, 1 to 2 creatives each, for 3 days.
- Kill an ad set if CTR is under 1% after a day, CPC is over $1 with no sales, or CPA is 2 to 3 times your target.
- Move ad sets with CTR above 1.5% and a profitable CPA into one CBO campaign with a budget of 3 to 5 times your target CPA.

      
## Video chapters
- 0:00 $376K in 25 days for a DTC skincare brand
- 1:05 Finding winning ads in the Meta Ads Library
- 2:38 The 5 to 8 second rule for your hook
- 4:08 How long an ad must run to count as a winner
- 6:28 Using Amazon reviews inside your ads
- 7:28 Carousel retargeting: selling routines and bundles
- 11:37 Our DTC Meta ads testing playbook
- 13:00 The 8 audience types we test
- 20:37 What to test in every ad
- 25:17 When to kill an ad set
- 26:55 Scaling winners into a CBO campaign
- 27:44 When to kill during scaling

      Meta Ads Library (Facebook Ads Library): A free transparency tool at facebook.com/ads/library that lists every ad currently running on Facebook, Instagram, Messenger and Audience Network, with the start date, platforms, creative versions and advertiser page. It does not show spend, reach or results for normal commercial ads outside the EU, and you do not need an ad account or a paid spy tool to use it.

      
        
## What is the Meta Ads Library?

        The Meta Ads Library (many people still call it the Facebook Ads Library) is a free tool from Meta that shows every ad currently running on Facebook, Instagram, Messenger and Audience Network. You can search by keyword or brand name, filter by country, and see the date each ad started running. You do not need an ad account, a Business Manager or even a Facebook login to use it.
For each ad you see the advertiser's page, the start date, the platforms it runs on and every creative version under the same ad. What you do not see for normal ecommerce ads in the US, UK, Canada or Australia is spend, impressions, CTR or ROAS. That is why media buyers read how long an ad has run, and how many versions a brand keeps live, as the signal for what is making money.
For a DTC brand it is the cheapest market research you can do: it shows you exactly which ads your biggest competitors keep paying for. The official tool lives at facebook.com/ads/library.

        
        
        
      
        
## How to find winning ads in the Meta Ads Library

        This is the exact process from the video, run for a DTC [skincare client](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/case-studies/skincare-beauty) selling a vitamin C serum.

        
        FilterBest setting for ecommerce researchWhyCountryYour main market (US, UK, CA, AU)Ads are localised; the US shows the most volumeAd categoryAll adsThe political category hides every commerce adActive statusActiveInactive ads include failed tests and old offersMedia typeVideo first, then imageVideo carries most DTC spend and shows the hookPlatformInstagram, then FacebookShows which placements the brand invests inDate rangeLast 90 daysSeparates proven evergreen ads from fresh tests
        
### 1. Search your product, not just your competitors
Open the Meta Ads Library, set the country to where your customers are (for our client, the United States), choose All ads and search for your product category. For this client we searched "vitamin C serum". This shows every brand advertising that product, including ones you did not know about.
If the category is stuck on Issues, elections or politics you will see no ecommerce ads at all. Switching it to All ads is the most common fix when the library looks empty.

### 2. Keep only ads that have run for 2 weeks or more
Every ad shows a Started running on date. Two weeks is enough to prove an ad, whether the brand spends $20 or $100 a day on it. If a big brand has kept an ad live for 2 to 3 months, it is profitable. An ad that started 12 days ago is not proven yet, so skip it.
Also check how many ads use the same creative. When a brand runs the same creative in 3 or more ads, it is scaling a winner.

### 3. Check the brand's own Facebook page too
One search does not always show everything. Open the brand's Facebook page and its Ad library link to see all of its active ads in one place, then open See ad details to count the versions of each concept and click through to the landing page behind it.

      
        
## The winning ad scorecard

        Because the library hides performance data, you infer it. Score every ad you save on these six signals; anything that scores 9 or more out of 12 goes into your next creative brief.

        
        SignalWhat to checkScore 0 to 2Run timeStarted running on date0: under 14 days, 1: 14 to 30 days, 2: 30+ daysVersionsSee ad details, version count0: one, 1: two to three, 2: four or moreDuplicationSame creative under several ads0: none, 1: two, 2: three or moreBrand activityNew ads from the page this week0: none, 1: one to two, 2: three or moreLanding pageDedicated page, bundle or offer0: generic product page, 1: offer on page, 2: dedicated pageCommentsEngagement on the ad post0: under 20, 1: 20 to 100, 2: 100+
        
      
        
## Why those ads work: 5 patterns we copied

        Finding a winner is half the job. The other half is understanding why it wins, so you copy the structure, not the ad.

        
        
        
### The message lands in 5 to 8 seconds
One winning vitamin C serum ad made its whole point in 6 seconds. Your hook has 5 to 8 seconds to stop the scroll and state the benefit. If you need to explain more, keep the full ad under 30 to 40 seconds.

### Trust comes first in skincare
The same ad opened with "recommended by US dermatologists". People are skeptical about putting a product they bought online on their skin. Proof (dermatologist recommended, clinically tested, verified reviews) answers that objection before it forms.

### Results without "before and after"
One winning ad showed hands at day 1 and day 30 without ever saying "before and after". Meta restricts before and after claims for personal health and beauty products, and ads that use them often get flagged. Show the change; do not label it.

### Amazon reviews inside the creative
Many DTC brands also sell on Amazon. One brand put a screenshot of a real Amazon review straight into the ad. Viewers who check Amazon find the same reviews, which removes the last doubt.

### Sell the routine, not the single product
A carousel [retargeting](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/blog/retargeting-for-dtc-brands) ad showed a full skincare routine: cleanser, vitamin C serum, retinol, soothing cream. Selling a routine lifts order value and works well with subscriptions. On our client's landing page we added "clinically recommended: 3 months for best results", so buyers choose the 3 month plan and stay long enough to see results.

      
        
## Our DTC Meta ads testing playbook

        Research only pays off when it turns into tests. We test at $20 per ad set. You can go down to $10 or up to $50 depending on your budget; this example assumes a brand that can spend $150 to $200 a day on testing.

        - Objective: conversions, optimised for purchase.
- $20 per ad set, 7 to 10 ad sets, 1 to 2 creatives per ad set.
- Run for 3 days. This is the validation phase.
- Checkpoints over 14 days: day 1, 4, 5, 7, 10 and 14.

        
        
      
        
## The 8 audience types we test

        Each ad set in the test targets one audience type. Combining interests this way keeps each ad set distinct, so Meta is not bidding against itself.

        
        Ad setWho it targetsSkincare exampleMagazineReaders of trade, lifestyle and category magazinesBeauty and skincare publicationsInformationalPeople learning about your category and its problemsSkincare blogs and education sitesCategoryInterest in the product type itselfAnti aging cream, cleanser, moisturizerPassionPeople passionate about the lifestyle around your productBeauty content consumersPopular groupFollowers of well known creators, experts and communitiesSkincare creators and communitiesSeedBuilt around your use case and ideal customerSunscreen, serum, premium vs budget buyersBuyersPages liked by people who praise competitor ads in the commentsBrands found on commenters' profilesBrandCompeting brands in your marketLarge beauty retailers and cosmetic brands
        
### How we find proven buyers from comments
Find a competitor ad with thousands of shares and positive comments. Open the profiles of people who say "I have used this brand for years" and look at the pages they like. Add those brands as interests in Ads Manager. These are people who already buy in your category.

### Audience size rules
- Keep each ad set close to, but under, 5 million people.
- Combine 2 to 3 interests from one group with 2 to 3 from another, then narrow with your main keyword to hit that size.
- Do not use the same keyword in more than 3 ad sets.

      
        
## What to test in every ad

        Change one element at a time across the ad sets, so you know which change moved the numbers.

        
        ElementWhat to testCreative conceptProduct demo, how to use, customer testimonial, founder story, benefit focusHook (first 3 seconds)Bold claim, question, problem statement, visual resultVisualsClose up, product in use, UGC video, lifestyle shot, unboxingAd copyConvenience, quality, value and identity anglesHeadlineShort, and name the offerOffer15% off first order, bundles, free shipping, buy more save more, 25% off subscriptionCall to actionShop now, discover the collection, explore the rangeSocial proofVerified reviews, Amazon review screenshotsFormatUGC video, static image, carousel, collection ad
        
      
        
## KPIs, test setup and when to kill an ad set

        Track the whole funnel, not just ROAS, so you can see where a losing ad set breaks.

        
        
        
### The KPIs we track
- Delivery: link clicks, CTR, CPC, CPM, landing page views, amount spent, frequency.
- Funnel: view content, add to cart and cost per add to cart, initiate checkout, cost per purchase.
- Revenue: purchase conversion value, ROAS, [average order value](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/aov).
- Video: 25%, 50%, 75% and 95% watch rates.

### When to kill an ad set
- CTR under 1% after a full day and $20 spent: people are not responding to the offer.
- CPC above $1 with no conversions.
- CPA at 2 to 3 times your target with no improvement.
- ROAS under your minimum (for this client, 2).
- Clicks but no view content events: people are not reaching the landing page.
- No meaningful action by day 3.

      
        
## Scaling winners into a CBO campaign

        Over the 14 day test you kill losers and keep 2 to 3 performers. Ad sets with CTR above 1.5% and a profitable CPA or positive ROAS move into one CBO (campaign budget optimization) campaign.

        - Put 3 to 5 proven ad sets in the CBO.
- Set the CBO budget at 3 to 5 times your target CPA. Example: target CPA $20, CBO budget about $100 a day.
- Keep scaling while the CBO stays profitable.

        
        
### When to pause or adjust the CBO
- CPA rises above 2 times your target.
- CTR drops by 1 point: a sign of [creative fatigue](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/creative-fatigue).
- ROAS falls below your minimum.
- Conversions drop on creatives that used to work: launch new iterations of the winning angle.

      
        
## The result: $376K in 25 days

        We used this exact process for a DTC skincare brand selling a vitamin C serum. In 25 days the brand did $376,000 in revenue and sold 2,508 units, around $150 per order. Results are from one client account, shared with permission. They are not typical and not a guarantee.
The method is repeatable even if your numbers are smaller: find ads that have survived 2 weeks, copy why they work rather than what they look like, test at $20 per ad set with clear kill rules, and only scale what has proven itself into a CBO. Need ad creatives to test? Our creative studio, SevenFigureStudio, makes [UGC video ads](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/viral-creatives) for DTC brands (link below).

        
        MetricResultRevenue$376,000Timeframe25 daysUnits sold2,508Average order valueAbout $150ProductVitamin C serum (DTC skincare)ChannelMeta ads (Facebook and Instagram)
        
      
        
## Searching the library like a media buyer

        Keyword searches that work for ecommerce. Search for offer language, not just product names: free shipping, bundle, limited drop, buy 2 get 1, 30 day guarantee. Combine with one niche word, for example bundle skincare or free shipping serum. Offer words surface ads that are built to convert.
Meta ad library search by ID. Every ad has a numeric Library ID shown on its card and in its URL. Set the search type to Ad ID and paste it to see that ad with all of its versions. Use this when a teammate or creator sends you a link.
Instagram only. Set the platform filter to Instagram. Vertical 9:16 Reels placements usually mean the brand has a creator led UGC pipeline, which is the fastest production model to copy.
Can you sort by impressions? Not for commercial ads. Sorting by impressions and spend ranges are only available for ads about social issues, elections or politics. Run time plus version count is the closest free proxy.

        
        
        
      
        
## Downloads, the API and when the library is not working

        Downloading videos. There is no download button. For internal research teams screen record the ad or save it with a browser tool. Keep it in a private swipe file and recreate the structure with your own product and footage; never re-upload a competitor's ad, footage or creators.
The Meta Ad Library API. It is free but limited: it covers ads about social issues, elections and politics plus EU transparency data, and needs a Meta developer account with confirmed identity. For ecommerce competitor research the web tool shows the same commercial ad fields, so most brands do not need the API.
When the library is not working, check these in order: the country is set to your market; the category is All ads; ad blockers and privacy extensions are off (try a private window); the search type matches what you pasted (Keyword vs Ad ID); and if nothing else works, Meta's tool may be down for a short time.

        
        
        
      
      
## Frequently Asked Questions

### Is the Meta Ads Library free?
Yes. The Meta Ads Library is free and public. You can search all active Facebook and Instagram ads without logging in or having an ad account.

### How long should an ad run before it counts as a winner?
At least 2 weeks. Brands do not keep paying for ads that lose money, so an ad running for 2 weeks or more, especially one used in several ads, is a strong winner signal.

### How much should I spend to test Meta ads?
We test at $20 per ad set across 7 to 10 ad sets for 3 days. You can start at $10 per ad set on a smaller budget, but you need enough spend for Meta to show results.

### When should I kill a Meta ad set?
Kill it if CTR is under 1% after a day, CPC is above $1 with no sales, or CPA stays at 2 to 3 times your target. If nothing meaningful happens by day 3, turn it off.

### Can I use before and after images in skincare ads?
Meta restricts before and after claims for personal health and beauty products, and these ads often get rejected. Show day 1 and day 30 visually instead of labelling it before and after.

### Can you see ad spend in the Meta Ads Library?
Not for normal commercial ads in the US, UK, Canada or Australia. Spend ranges and impressions are shown only for ads about social issues, elections or politics, and ads delivered in the EU show reach data.

### Can I search the Meta Ads Library by ad ID?
Yes. Set the search type to Ad ID and paste the numeric Library ID from the ad card or its URL to see that ad with all of its versions.

### What is a CBO campaign in Meta ads?
CBO (campaign budget optimization, now called Advantage campaign budget) sets one budget at campaign level and lets Meta move it to the best ad sets. We move 3 to 5 proven ad sets into a CBO with a budget of 3 to 5 times target CPA.
