# TikTok GMV Max: How It Works, ROI Targets and Why It Will Not Spend
URL: https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/blog/tiktok-gmv-max
Summary: TikTok GMV Max explained: Product vs LIVE GMV Max, setting a target ROI from your margins, Max delivery, attribution and what to do when it will not spend.

Direct Answer: GMV Max is TikTok Shop's automated ad campaign type. You choose the products (Product GMV Max) or the LIVE stream (LIVE GMV Max), set a budget and a target ROI, and TikTok decides which videos, placements and audiences to use to drive the most gross merchandise value. According to TikTok's help center, it has been the default and only campaign type for new TikTok Shop ads since July 2025. Set the ROI target at or above your break-even, feed it plenty of creator videos, and lower the target slightly if it will not spend.

      
      GMV Max: An automated TikTok Shop ad campaign that optimizes for gross merchandise value (GMV), the total value of orders before fees. It uses your shop's product videos, authorized affiliate creator posts and product cards, and aims to hit the return on ad spend you set as a target ROI.

      
        
## What GMV Max is and what it replaced

        GMV Max is the campaign type TikTok now uses for almost all paid [TikTok Shop](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tiktok-shop-agency) advertising. Instead of building ad groups and audiences, you give it products or a LIVE room, a daily budget and a target ROI. TikTok then spends across its Shop ad placements using whatever content it can access for those products.
As of November 2026, TikTok's help center article on the GMV Max migration says that since July 2025 advertisers using the Sales objective with TikTok Shop as the destination can no longer create, edit or duplicate Product Shopping Ads, Video Shopping Ads or LIVE Shopping Ads. Existing campaigns could keep running, and upgraded campaigns started from their historical ROI. TikTok says Video Shopping Ads remain available with Showcase as the destination, and LIVE Shopping Ads can still be created with a TikTok account identity rather than a shop.
Two setup rules trip people up: the ad account, TikTok accounts and shop must sit in the same Business Center, and a product in GMV Max cannot also run in standard Shop ads. Availability also varies by market, so check the [TikTok Ads](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tiktok-ads-agency) help center for your country.

        
        
        
      
        
## Product GMV Max vs LIVE GMV Max

        Product GMV Max promotes chosen products all day using short videos and product cards. LIVE GMV Max drives viewers into a LIVE stream while it is on air and optimizes for the revenue the stream makes. Most brands start with Product GMV Max and add LIVE GMV Max once they run LIVE on a steady schedule.

        
        Product GMV MaxLIVE GMV MaxWhat it promotesSelected products from your shopA LIVE stream from a linked TikTok accountWhen it runsAlways on, for as long as the campaign is activeAround LIVE sessionsCreative it usesShop videos, authorized affiliate creator posts and product cardsThe stream itself, plus short videos that send viewers into the LIVE (TikTok calls these Video-to-live and Live-to-live)What ROI measuresGross revenue from the selected products divided by ad costTotal LIVE room gross revenue divided by ad cost, according to TikTokBest forHero products with lots of video content and sales historyBrands with a regular LIVE schedule and a host who can sellMain riskReported ROI includes organic orders, so it can look better than paid performance really isSpend during weak streams, and results tied to host quality
        
### Which one to start with
Start with Product GMV Max on a few hero products that already sell and already have creator videos. LIVE GMV Max only pays off when the stream itself converts, so prove that organically first.

      
        
## Target ROI vs Max delivery

        GMV Max has two main ways to spend. Target ROI tries to keep your return close to a number you set. Max delivery tries to spend the whole budget and treats ROI as secondary. TikTok's help center describes Max delivery as something you can turn on for individual products inside a Product GMV Max campaign, and TikTok keeps adding options, so the exact names in your account may differ.

        
        OptionWhat it doesWhen to use itWhat to watchTarget ROIAims to keep return near your target. A lower target lets it spend more, a higher target restricts spend.The default for most brands. Use it whenever profit per order matters.A target set above your history often means very little spend.Max deliverySpends the budget first and optimizes ROI second, so ROI can swing.Product launches, sale events or pushing a proven product for more volume.TikTok's own guidance suggests a budget of 1 to 5 times what the product spends on Target ROI, and warns that going above 5 times can cut ROI sharply.Growth autopilotA newer option TikTok describes for Product GMV Max that works to a 7-day ROI target and 7-day budget.Brands that want smoother weekly pacing.TikTok advises against changing the target mid-cycle. Check the help center, as this is still changing.
        
### ROI protection
TikTok's help center describes ROI protection for some Target ROI campaigns: if ROI falls below 90% of the daily target, TikTok may issue ad credits. Eligibility rules apply and change, so check the current article. It softens a bad day but does not make an unprofitable target profitable.

      
        
## How to set your ROI target from unit economics

        Set your GMV Max target ROI at or above your [TikTok Shop break-even ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tools/tiktok-shop-break-even-roas-calculator), never below it. GMV Max ROI is gross revenue divided by ad cost, which is the same maths as ROAS. [Break-even ROAS](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/tools/break-even-roas-calculator) is the price of the product divided by the profit you make on one order before ads. If you spend more than that profit to win the order, you lose money.
Here is an illustrative example with made-up numbers. A product sells for $40. Product cost is $10, shipping and packing is $6, the TikTok Shop referral fee comes to $3.20 and the affiliate commission is $6. Profit before ads is $40 minus $25.20, which is $14.80. Break-even ROAS is $40 divided by $14.80, which is about 2.7. Any ROI target below 2.7 loses money on every ad-driven order.
Our free calculator does this for you: enter your price, costs, referral fee and commission, and it shows profit per order and the break-even number.

        - Start at break-even or a little above it. Below break-even you are buying revenue at a loss, unless you have a clear plan to earn it back through repeat orders.
- Compare it with TikTok's recommendation. TikTok suggests a starting ROI based on your history, calculated as historical non-LIVE GMV divided by historical ad cost. If that number is well below your break-even, the product needs better margins, a higher price or better content before more spend.
- Allow for organic orders. Reported GMV Max ROI includes organic orders for the same products, so the true paid return is lower than the dashboard shows. A target a little above break-even gives you a safety margin.
- Use [contribution margin](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/glossary/contribution-margin), not gross margin: fees, shipping, returns and commission all come out before ads.

        
        
      
        
## Why GMV Max is not spending

        The most common reason GMV Max under-spends is a target ROI set higher than the product has achieved before. TikTok's own guidance treats low budget use as a sign that the target is too high, not as a delivery fault. The fix is usually to lower the target a little, then wait.

        - ROI target too high. Lower it in small steps toward TikTok's recommended ROI, as long as it stays at or above your break-even. TikTok advises against changing it many times a day.
- Too little content. GMV Max can only spend when it has videos to show. One or two videos per product gives it very little to work with.
- Weak product page or price. A low conversion rate means each impression earns less, so the campaign cannot hit your target and holds back.
- New shop or new product. With little sales history, TikTok has less data to predict who will buy. Expect slow, uneven spend for the first days.
- Products locked elsewhere. A product already running in other Shop ads, or not set up correctly in the same Business Center, may not deliver in GMV Max.
- Changes made too soon. Every edit gives the system less time to settle. TikTok's troubleshooting guidance suggests watching new or adjusted campaigns for 2 to 3 days.

        
        
### What not to do
Raising the budget will not fix under-spending: a campaign that cannot spend at your target will not spend more just because the budget is bigger. And do not drop the target far below break-even just to get spend moving.

      
        
## How creator and affiliate videos feed GMV Max

        GMV Max is only as good as the content it can choose from. According to TikTok's help center, Product GMV Max automatically includes authorized affiliate videos that feature your selected products, under the source TikTok labels "Affiliate post". Those videos receive a commercial content label. If a strong creator video is missing, you can ask the creator for authorization or add it with its video code.
So your [affiliate program](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/blog/dtc-affiliate-program) is also your ad creative pipeline. Every creator video gives GMV Max another option to test, which is why creator seeding and samples belong in the ad budget.

        - Keep a steady flow of new videos for each hero product, from your own account and from creators.
- Cover different angles: demonstrations, problem and solution, unboxing, comparisons and honest reviews.
- Use exclusion filters to stop paid delivery on videos that are off-brand or make claims you would not approve.
- Check which videos earn the most gross revenue each week and brief more creators on those angles.

        
        
      
        
## How GMV Max counts organic and affiliate sales

        GMV Max gives itself credit for more than ad-driven sales, so read its numbers with care. TikTok's help center on GMV Max attribution says that while a Product GMV Max campaign runs, orders for its selected products are attributed to the campaign, including organic orders from people who did not view or click an ad. Orders from affiliate videos featuring those products also roll in. For ad-driven orders, TikTok counts purchases within one day of a view or click.
So reported ROI looks higher than the paid return really is, GMV Max can appear to "take over" sales that were already happening, and comparing its ROI with your Meta ROAS is not like for like.
TikTok itself recommends judging products and videos on gross revenue, because ROI and cost per order mix paid and organic orders. The better test is the whole shop: total TikTok Shop revenue and profit against total ad spend, before and after a change. If both go up, the campaign is adding sales. If revenue stays flat while ad spend rises, GMV Max is mostly claiming sales you would have had anyway.

        
        
        
### Where to go from here
GMV Max changes quickly, so check the TikTok Ads help center for current names and limits before big changes. Our TikTok Shop strategy guide covers the listings, pricing and LIVE selling that feed it, and our TikTok Shop agency team can run it for you, starting with a [Brand Growth Audit](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/book).

      
      
## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is GMV Max on TikTok?
GMV Max is TikTok Shop's automated ad campaign type. You choose products or a LIVE stream, set a budget and a target ROI, and TikTok picks the videos, placements and audiences to drive the most gross merchandise value. According to TikTok's help center, it has been the default campaign type for new TikTok Shop ads since July 2025.

### What is the difference between Product GMV Max and LIVE GMV Max?
Product GMV Max promotes selected products all day using shop videos, affiliate creator posts and product cards. LIVE GMV Max sends viewers into a LIVE stream while it is on air and optimizes for the revenue the stream makes. Most brands start with Product GMV Max.

### What target ROI should I set for GMV Max?
Set it at or above your break-even ROAS, which is your price divided by your profit per order before ads. Compare that with TikTok's recommended ROI, which is based on your history. If the recommendation is below break-even, fix margins, pricing or content before adding spend.

### Why is my GMV Max campaign not spending?
Usually because the target ROI is higher than the product has achieved before. Other causes are too few videos, a weak product page or price, a new shop with little history, or frequent edits. Lower the target slightly, stay at or above break-even, and give it 2 to 3 days.

### Does GMV Max take credit for organic sales?
Yes. TikTok's help center says orders for the selected products during a Product GMV Max campaign are attributed to it, including organic and affiliate orders. Reported ROI is therefore higher than the true paid return, so judge it on total shop revenue and profit against total ad spend.

      
## Sources

# DTC Ecommerce Case Study: $376,000 in 25 Days
URL: https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/376000-25-days-dtc-client-meta-ads
Summary: A DTC client made $376,000 in 25 days from Meta Ads during Q4. Covers the approach and what the team changed. Read the full breakdown of the account.

A DTC client made $376,000 in 25 days from Meta Ads during Q4. The Ads Manager view in the video covers 1 to 25 October 2026 and totals $376,256.68 in purchase conversion value from 2,508 purchases, an average of about $150 per purchase and roughly $15,000 a day. The top ad set alone brought 661 purchases worth $99,206.68, and the next one 553 purchases worth $82,950. The post does not give ad spend or ROAS. The method, finding winning creatives, testing them and scaling the winners, is covered in a full live breakdown on YouTube.

        Write-up by [Gaurav Kapoor](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/about), Founder, Brand Scaling · Updated 2026-11-16

        
## Results at a Glance

        NicheDTC ecommerceRevenue$376,000Timeframe25 daysOrders2,508ChannelMeta ads (Facebook & Instagram)ProofScreen recording
        
## The Approach
Find winning creatives, test them against each other, then move budget into the winners and scale them through Q4.

## What We Did
- Searched for winning creative angles before spending at scale.
- Tested the creatives and kept only the ones that proved themselves.
- Scaled the winning ad sets: the top two brought 1,214 of the 2,508 purchases.
- Recorded the full process as a live breakdown on YouTube.
Result: $376,256.68 in Meta purchase value from 2,508 purchases between 1 and 25 October 2026 (ad spend and ROAS not stated).

        
## Key Takeaways
- Q4 IS IN FULL SWING, AND WE’RE SCALING HARD!
- I’m dropping a full YouTube breakdown on how we found winning creatives, tested them, and scaled the winners.
- What niche are you scaling this Q4?
- Meta Ads, Facebook Ads Strategy, DTC Brand Scaling, Shopify Store Growth, Ecommerce Scaling, Skincare Brand Marketing, Q4 Ecommerce Strategy, Winning Ad Creatives, Meta Ads Case Study

        
## Original Post: $376,000 in just 25 days for one of our DTC clients using Meta Ads
Q4 IS IN FULL SWING, AND WE’RE SCALING HARD! $376,000 in just 25 days for one of our DTC Client using Meta Ads!
I’m dropping a full YouTube breakdown on how we found winning creatives, tested them, and scaled the winners.

# Fitness Case Study: $307,950 in 30 Days
URL: https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/307950-revenue-fitness-brand-2053-units-30-days
Summary: A DTC fitness brand made $307,950 in revenue from 2,053 units sold over the last 30 days, shown in the Meta Ads Manager view in the video.

A DTC fitness brand made $307,950 in revenue from 2,053 units sold over the last 30 days, shown in the Meta Ads Manager view in the video. That is an average of exactly $150 per purchase ($307,950 divided by 2,053) and about $10,265 a day. One ad set carried most of the volume: 1,198 purchases worth $179,700, about 58% of the total. The post frames the result as Q4 preparation for fitness brands. It does not give ad spend or ROAS.

        Write-up by [Gaurav Kapoor](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/about), Founder, Brand Scaling · Updated 2026-11-16

        
## Results at a Glance

        NicheFitness brandRevenue$307,950Timeframe30 daysOrders2,053ChannelMeta ads (Facebook & Instagram)ProofScreen recording
        
## The Approach
Put most of the budget behind the ad set that proves itself, while smaller ad sets keep testing, ahead of Q4.
Result: $307,950 in revenue and 2,053 units sold in 30 days for a DTC fitness brand on Meta Ads (ad spend and ROAS not stated).

# DTC Ecommerce Case Study: $1M in 6 Months
URL: https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/finally-scale-client-almost-1m-sales-6-months
Summary: A client store scaled to almost $1 million in sales within six months of launch. Covers what the team changed. See the numbers and what drove them.

A client store scaled to almost $1 million in sales within six months of launch. The post is a video proof of the Shopify and Meta dashboards; the system behind it was aggressive creative testing early, then budget consolidation onto the two winning concepts once cost per purchase stabilised.

        Write-up by [Gaurav Kapoor](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/about), Founder, Brand Scaling · Updated 2026-11-03

        
## Results at a Glance

        NicheDTC ecommerceRevenue$1MTimeframe6 monthsChannelMeta ads (Facebook & Instagram)ProofScreen recording
        
## What We Did
- Tested a wide matrix of hooks and angles in the first 60 days to find the winning concept.
- Consolidated spend onto the winners with broad targeting and cost controls.
- Kept weekly creative iterations running so the account did not plateau at month four.
Result: Close to $1M in sales inside six months, 4.6x ROAS at scale.

# Dropshipping Case Study: $449,221 in 49 Days
URL: https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/449221-last-49-days-newer-client-dropshipping-brands-starting
Summary: A newer dropshipping client generated $449,221 in 49 days during the Q4 run-up. Covers what the team changed. See the numbers and what drove them.

A newer dropshipping client generated $449,221 in 49 days during the Q4 run-up. The post shares the dashboard and the product philosophy behind it: products already proven from $10K days to $100K months, scaled with simple broad campaigns rather than complex targeting.

        Write-up by [Gaurav Kapoor](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/about), Founder, Brand Scaling · Updated 2026-11-03

        
## Results at a Glance

        NicheDropshipping storeRevenue$449,221Timeframe49 daysChannelMeta ads (Facebook & Instagram)ProofDashboard screenshot
        
## What We Did
- Launched proven problem-solving products rather than untested trends.
- Ran broad targeting with automatic bidding from day one, adding manual bids only on consistent winners.
- Prepared creative and offers in advance of Q4 so scale came from the calendar, not panic.
Result: $449,221 in 49 days at 4.2x ROAS.

# Dropshipping Case Study: $148K in 1 Day
URL: https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/cases/148k-day-best-day-whole-career-ending-up-phenomenal
Summary: A client store recorded $148,000 in sales in a single day and closed the month at $294,000 with a 37% net margin. Covers what the team changed.

A client store recorded $148,000 in sales in a single day and closed the month at $294,000 with a 37% net margin. The post explains the method: a general store tested 25 products, six showed promise and one proved a consistent winner, after which the store was niched around that product and scaled with automatic bidding and broad targeting.

        Write-up by [Gaurav Kapoor](https://www.brandscalinghacks.com/about), Founder, Brand Scaling · Updated 2026-11-03

        
## Results at a Glance

        NicheDropshipping storeRevenue$148KTimeframeone dayMargin37%ChannelMeta ads (Facebook & Instagram)ProofScreen recording
        
## What We Did
- Tested 25 products through a data-driven process and identified one consistent winner.
- Niched the entire store around the winning product's category once it proved itself.
- Used automatic bidding and broad targeting first, adding manual bids only once consistency was clear.
Result: $148K in one day, $294K month, 37% net margin.

        
## Key Takeaways
- Utilize Automatic Bidding & Broad Targeting right off the bat!
- Utilize Manual Bidding Early only if you notice massive consistency towards the offer!
- Learn the CORRECT way to do INTELLIGENT PRODUCT RESEARCH! -- Stop relying on Spy-Tools & Apps to find your products, DO IT YOURSELF THE SIX-FIGURE WAY!

        
## Original Post: $148K in One Day - The Best Day in my Whole Career! Ending Up this Phenomenal Mont...
$148K in One Day - The Best Day in my Whole Career! Ending Up this Phenomenal Month With $294K a 37% Margin
I like to think that the bags under my eyes represent how hard I’ve worked these past years lol
It takes only 1 winning product to make 6 or 7 figures in this business...
If you don’t have a winning product, you’ll be burning money - and spending more than you make, scratching your head - wondering while it’s not working.
When you have a winning product, you can literally do NO wrong.
In fact, with winning products, most of the time... You can scale it EXTREMELY efficiently!
A winner is a winner!
The KEY to any successful business is CONSISTENCY.
Being consistent is one of the most vital and surefire ways to continually grow a successful business, however, it is also something that is often overlooked...
Takeaways:
1.) We ran General Store for this client with 25 potential products using our data-driven process & we found around 6 great winners out of which we noticed massive profitability in a consistent way on one out of 6 products that proved itself a real winner. Remember when I say ONCE you find a winner, the entire store should be niched around the niche of the winning product, this is how we did for this client!
2.) Utilize Automatic Bidding & Broad Targeting right off the bat!
3.) Don't become discouraged!! Learn the PROPER methods, strategies, and knowledge necessary to MAKE THIS EASY! -- People are teaching outdated tactics; STOP LISTENING TO THE WRONG PEOPLE!!
4.) Utilize Manual Bidding Early only if you notice massive consistency towards the offer!
